question: Under Section 46(1) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what is the maximum duration for which the Central Government can supersede the Council at any one time?
options: For up to five (5) years, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
For up to ten (10) years, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Permanently with no reconstitution.
For a period not exceeding one (1) year.
explanationCorrect: Section 46(1) provides: '...supersede the Council for such period, not exceeding one year, as may be specified in the notification.'
explanationIncorrect: The statutory maximum period of Council supersession is 1 year.

question: Under Section 55 of the Actuaries Act 2006, who holds the statutory power to make rules for carrying out the provisions of the Act?
options: The High Court of Judicature at Bombay, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The Council of the Institute of Actuaries of India.
The Central Government, by notification in the Official Gazette.
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India.
explanationCorrect: Section 55 explicitly grants rule-making power to the Central Government by notification in the Official Gazette.
explanationIncorrect: Rules are framed by the Central Government under Section 55; Regulations are framed by Council under Section 56.

question: Under Section 56 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what two conditions must be satisfied before regulations made by the Council can acquire the force of law?
options: Prior approval of the Central Government and publication in the Official Gazette.
Concurrence of the Governor of Maharashtra and the Mayor of Mumbai.
Approval of 75% of Fellows voting by postal ballot, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Approval of the Bar Council of India, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 56 mandates that regulations made by Council require prior approval of Central Government and notification in the Official Gazette.
explanationIncorrect: Prior Central Government sanction and Gazette notification are non-negotiable statutory prerequisites.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 1
question: An actuary in practice permits an unqualified friend who runs an IT consultancy to issue actuarial valuation reports under the actuary's official letterhead and stamp. Under Part I, Clause (1) of the First Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, what is the legal character of this act?
options: A minor commercial dispute with no professional implications, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Professional misconduct in practice: an actuary allows any person to practice in their name as an actuary unless such person is also an actuary and in partnership with or employed by them.
Permissible subcontracting under standard IT outsourcing guidelines.
Permitted provided the fee is shared 50-50, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Clause (1), Part I of the First Schedule deems an actuary guilty of professional misconduct if they allow any person to practice in their name as an actuary unless that person is also an actuary and in partnership with or employed by them.
explanationIncorrect: Lending one's professional name to unqualified individuals is strictly professional misconduct under Clause 1.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 2
question: A consulting actuary enters into an agreement with a chartered accountant whereby the actuary pays the CA a 15% commission for every corporate gratuity valuation client referred to the actuary. Under Part I, Clause (2) of the First Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, how is this treated?
options: Professional misconduct: an actuary pays or agrees to pay or share any portion of fees or profits of their professional business with any person other than an actuary or partner.
Legitimate referral fee sharing standard in financial services, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Permitted provided the payment is made via bank transfer with GST, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Permitted if the client signs a consent waiver, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Clause (2), Part I of the First Schedule prohibits an actuary from paying or sharing any portion of professional fees or profits with any person other than a member of the Institute or partner.
explanationIncorrect: Paying referral commissions or kickbacks to non-actuaries is prohibited professional misconduct.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 3
question: An actuary in practice accepts a 20% cut of legal fees from a litigation law firm in exchange for referring motor third-party insurance claimants to that firm. Under Part I, Clause (3) of the First Schedule, how is this characterized?
options: Professional misconduct: an actuary accepts or agrees to accept any part of the profits of the professional work of a lawyer, broker, or other person who is not a member of the Institute.
Permitted as ancillary income under the Indian Income Tax Act, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Permitted if the actuary donates half the fee to charity, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
A standard cross-selling partnership recognized by the IRDAI, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Clause (3), Part I of the First Schedule prohibits an actuary from accepting any part of the fees or profits from the work of a lawyer, auctioneer, broker, or other non-member.
explanationIncorrect: Accepting referral kickbacks from third parties compromises professional independence and constitutes misconduct.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 4
question: A consulting actuary forms a partnership firm with a non-actuary data scientist to offer joint actuarial pricing and software development services. Under Part I, Clause (4) of the First Schedule, does this violate the Actuaries Act 2006?
options: Yes, but only if the data scientist earns higher profits than the actuary, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

No; multi-disciplinary partnerships are automatically permitted without Council recognition, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
No; because data science is closely related to actuarial science, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Yes; an actuary is guilty of professional misconduct if they enter into partnership with any person other than an actuary in practice or person possessing qualifications recognized by the Council.
explanationCorrect: Clause (4), Part I of the First Schedule prohibits an actuary in practice from entering into partnership with any person other than an actuary in practice or person possessing qualifications recognized by Council.
explanationIncorrect: Unapproved partnerships with non-actuaries violate statutory partnership rules.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clauses 5 & 6
question: A consulting actuary hires an advertising agency to place aggressive billboards on highways and sends unsolicited commercial emails to corporate HR directors offering 'Cheapest Gratuity Valuation Guaranteed'. Under Part I, Clauses (5) and (6) of the First Schedule, how is this viewed?
options: Permitted as long as the claim of being cheapest is true, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Permitted if the actuary includes their photo on the billboard, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Standard commercial marketing protected by constitutional freedom of trade, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Professional misconduct: an actuary secures professional business through non-member agents or solicits clients/professional work through advertisements or circulars contrary to Council guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Clauses (5) and (6), Part I of the First Schedule prohibit securing business through unqualified intermediaries or soliciting clients/advertising professional work contrary to Council guidelines.
explanationIncorrect: Aggressive commercial solicitation and price-undercutting advertisements constitute professional misconduct.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 8
question: An actuary is offered an appointment as statutory Appointed Actuary of an insurance company to replace a predecessor actuary who resigned over valuation disputes. Under Part I, Clause (8) of the First Schedule, what must the incoming actuary do before accepting?
options: Demand that the insurer pay a 50% advance fee, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Communicate in writing with the retiring actuary to ascertain whether there are any professional reasons why the appointment should not be accepted.
Accept immediately to avoid losing the consulting fee to a competitor, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
File a caveat in the High Court against the retiring actuary, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Clause (8), Part I of the First Schedule requires an actuary in practice to communicate in writing with the previous actuary before accepting a position previously held by another member.
explanationIncorrect: Prior professional communication with the predecessor actuary is mandatory to protect professional independence.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 9
question: A consulting actuary signs an independent valuation report on the defined benefit pension obligations of a company in which the actuary owns a 25% equity interest, without disclosing this interest. Under Part I, Clause (9) of the First Schedule, how is this treated?
options: A matter strictly between the shareholder and the registrar of companies, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Permissible if the shares were inherited from ancestors, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Permissible provided the actuary valued the liabilities accurately, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Professional misconduct: an actuary expresses an opinion or signs a report on actuarial work where the actuary, their firm, or partner has a substantial interest, without disclosing such interest.
explanationCorrect: Clause (9), Part I of the First Schedule prohibits an actuary from expressing an opinion or certifying work in which they or their firm have a substantial financial interest without full disclosure.
explanationIncorrect: Undisclosed financial interests destroy professional objectivity and independence.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part II
question: Under Part II of the First Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, what constitutes professional misconduct in relation to an actuary in salaried employment?
options: Paying or agreeing to pay any portion of their salary to non-members, or accepting any part of fees or gains directly or indirectly from a lawyer, agent, or client by way of commission or kickback.
Taking maternity or paternity leave, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Asking for a promotion or annual salary increment from their employer, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Resigning with 3 months' notice to join another insurance company, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Part II, Clauses (1) and (2) of the First Schedule penalize employed actuaries who share salary with non-members or accept secret commissions/kickbacks from lawyers, agents, or clients.
explanationIncorrect: Secret commissions or fee-splitting by employed actuaries violate professional integrity in employment.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part III
question: Under Part III of the First Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, which of the following acts constitutes 'General Misconduct' applicable to all members (whether in practice or employment)?
options: Not being a Fellow, acts as an actuary; or does not supply information called for, or fails to comply with requirements asked for, by the Institute, Council, or Committees.
Traveling abroad on vacation without informing the President, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Failing to attend an alumni dinner, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Buying shares of an insurance company in the secondary stock market, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Part III, Clauses (1) and (2) of the First Schedule treat as general misconduct: falsely acting as an actuary when not a Fellow, or failing to supply information or comply with requirements of the Institute/Committees.
explanationIncorrect: Refusing to cooperate with Institute inquiries constitutes statutory general misconduct.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part IV
question: Under Part IV of the First Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, what is 'Other Misconduct' in relation to members of the Institute?
options: Eating lunch at a desk instead of the cafeteria, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

A member is guilty of other misconduct if convicted by a competent court of an offense punishable with imprisonment for a term not exceeding six months, or in the opinion of Council has brought disrepute to the profession.
Failure to pass an actuarial exam on the first attempt, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Disagreeing with a colleague during an academic seminar, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Part IV of the First Schedule defines other misconduct: conviction for offenses punishable with imprisonment up to 6 months, or actions bringing disrepute to the profession or Institute.
explanationIncorrect: Bringing the profession into disrepute or minor criminal convictions fall under Part IV.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 1
question: An Appointed Actuary of an insurance company intentionally discloses confidential policyholder claims data and proprietary pricing algorithms to a competing insurer without client consent. Under Part I, Clause (1) of the Second Schedule, how is this treated?
options: Grave professional misconduct: an actuary discloses information acquired in the course of professional engagement to any person other than the client without client consent, unless required by law.
A breach of commercial contract but not professional misconduct, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Permitted provided the actuary was paid a consulting fee by the competitor, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Permitted under the doctrine of industry best practice sharing, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Clause (1), Part I of the Second Schedule makes unauthorized disclosure of confidential professional information a grave offense subject to the Disciplinary Committee's jurisdiction.
explanationIncorrect: Confidentiality is a fundamental duty under the Second Schedule; unauthorized disclosure attracts severe penalties.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 7
question: An actuary certifies statutory solvency and reserving reports for an insurer without performing basic data reconciliation, ignoring massive claims backlogs resulting in an understatement of reserves by Rs. 500 Crores. Under Part I, Clause (7) of the Second Schedule, how is this characterized?
options: A harmless clerical error that can be rectified in the subsequent quarter, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Grave professional misconduct: an actuary is guilty of gross negligence in the conduct of their professional duties.
The exclusive liability of the insurer's IT data entry clerks, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
A matter protected by the actuary's freedom of opinion, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Clause (7), Part I of the Second Schedule explicitly designates 'gross negligence in the conduct of professional duties' as grave professional misconduct tried by the Disciplinary Committee.
explanationIncorrect: Gross negligence causing massive reserve misstatements is a premier Second Schedule offense punishable by permanent removal.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 9
question: A consulting actuary prepares an actuarial report for a client that departs radically from mandatory Actuarial Practice Standards (APS) issued by the Council, but deliberately omits any mention of this departure in the report. Under Part I, Clause (9) of the Second Schedule, what is the consequence?
options: Permitted if the actuary believes the standards are outdated, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
No consequence; practice standards are purely advisory suggestions, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Permitted as long as the client did not ask about departures, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Professional misconduct: an actuary fails to invite attention to any material departure from the generally accepted procedure of actuarial work or standards applicable to the circumstances.
explanationCorrect: Clause (9), Part I of the Second Schedule mandates inviting attention to material departures from generally accepted procedures and practice standards; concealing departures is grave misconduct.
explanationIncorrect: Concealing departures from mandatory standards violates statutory disclosure duties.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 10
question: An actuary receives client funds deposited in trust to pay statutory fees to the Institute, but misappropriates the funds to finance personal stock market day-trading. Under Part I, Clause (10) of the Second Schedule, how is this treated?
options: A private commercial borrowing with standard interest obligations, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Grave professional misconduct: an actuary fails to keep moneys of a client in a separate banking account or uses such moneys for purposes other than intended.
An internal administrative matter outside Institute jurisdiction, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Permitted if the actuary makes a profit and returns the principal, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Clause (10), Part I of the Second Schedule penalizes failure to maintain separate client accounts or misappropriating client moneys as grave professional misconduct.
explanationIncorrect: Mishandling or misappropriating client trust funds attracts severe disciplinary and criminal liability.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part II
question: Under Part II of the Second Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, what constitutes 'General Misconduct' triable by the Disciplinary Committee?
options: A member submitting an expense claim with a missing taxi receipt, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
A member failing to attend two consecutive general meetings, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
A member publishing an editorial disagreeing with government economic policy, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

A member is guilty of general misconduct if they contravene any of the provisions of the Act, rules, regulations, or guidelines, or are convicted by a competent court of an offense punishable with imprisonment exceeding six months.
explanationCorrect: Part II of the Second Schedule penalizes contraventions of the Act/rules/regulations, or criminal convictions punishable with imprisonment exceeding 6 months, as grave general misconduct.
explanationIncorrect: Statutory violations and major criminal convictions fall under Second Schedule Part II.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part III
question: Under Part III of the Second Schedule to the Actuaries Act 2006, what is 'Other Misconduct' that empowers the Disciplinary Committee to impose sanctions up to permanent expulsion?
options: A member changing their residential address without written notice, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
A member losing an umbrella in the Institute lobby, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
A member failing to register for an annual conference, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
A member is guilty of other misconduct if convicted by a competent court of any offense involving moral turpitude punishable with imprisonment for a term exceeding six months.
explanationCorrect: Part III of the Second Schedule addresses serious criminal convictions (moral turpitude with imprisonment exceeding 6 months) as other misconduct triable by the Disciplinary Committee.
explanationIncorrect: Major criminal convictions involving moral turpitude warrant permanent removal from the register.

question: Where an offense under Chapter V of the Actuaries Act 2006 has been committed by a company, who is deemed guilty of the offense under Section 40(1)?
options: Every person who, at the time the offense was committed, was in charge of, and was responsible to the company for the conduct of the business, as well as the company itself.
No person can be held liable because a company is a separate legal person, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Only the security guard stationed at the front gate, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Only the junior-most administrative clerk who typed the report.
explanationCorrect: Section 40(1) enacts corporate vicarious liability: every person in charge and responsible for the conduct of the company's business, as well as the company, is deemed guilty unless they prove lack of knowledge or due diligence.
explanationIncorrect: Corporate officers in charge of business bear statutory liability for corporate offenses.

question: Under the Proviso to Section 40(1) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what statutory defense is available to a director or manager prosecuted for a corporate offense?
options: Proving that the actuary was on annual leave on the date of filing, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Proving that the offense was committed without their knowledge or that they exercised all due diligence to prevent the commission of such offense.
Proving that the company made a financial donation to the ruling political party, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Proving that they hold dual citizenship in an overseas nation, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: The Proviso to Section 40(1) provides a safe-harbour defense if the individual proves the offense occurred without knowledge or that due diligence was exercised.
explanationIncorrect: Lack of knowledge and active due diligence are standard corporate criminal defenses.

question: Under Section 40(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, if an offense is proved to have been committed with the consent or connivance of, or attributable to neglect by, a director, manager, or secretary, what is the consequence?
options: Such director, manager, secretary, or other officer shall also be deemed guilty of that offense and liable to be proceeded against and punished accordingly.
The prosecution is transferred to the consumer dispute redressal commission, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
The company pays a 5% surcharge and the officer is immunized, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The officer is given a warning letter with no criminal liability, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 40(2) holds directors, managers, and officers personally liable if the offense is attributable to their consent, connivance, or neglect.
explanationIncorrect: Personal culpability for corporate fraud cannot hide behind the corporate veil.

question: Under Section 49 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what status is conferred upon members of the Council, members of the Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee, QRB, and officers of the Institute?
options: They are deemed to be public servants within the meaning of Section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).
They are judicial magistrates of the second class, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
They are private commercial employees with no public status, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
They are officers of the United Nations, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Section 49 explicitly enacts: 'The Chairperson, Presiding Officer, members and other officers of the Authority, Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee and Council shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code.'
explanationIncorrect: Public servant status under IPC Section 21 provides legal authority and attaches anti-corruption statutes.

question: Under Section 48 of the Actuaries Act 2006, how are vacancies, defects in constitution, or irregularities in election to the Council or committees treated regarding the validity of their acts?
options: All acts and resolutions passed during a period of vacancy are void ab initio, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
All membership certificates issued become invalid immediately, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Any member can declare all Institute decisions null and void, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.

No act or proceeding of the Council or committees shall be called in question merely on the ground of any vacancy in, or defect in the constitution of the Council/committee, or defect in election/nomination.
explanationCorrect: Section 48 enacts the standard validation clause: acts of Council or committees are not invalidated merely due to vacancies, defects in constitution, or irregularities in election.
explanationIncorrect: The validation clause ensures administrative continuity and legal certainty.

question: Under Section 50 of the Actuaries Act 2006, does a Civil Court have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Council, Disciplinary Committee, or Appellate Authority is empowered to determine?
options: No civil court shall have jurisdiction to entertain any suit or proceeding in respect of any matter which the Council, Board of Discipline, Disciplinary Committee or Appellate Authority is empowered by or under this Act to determine.
Yes; provided the plaintiff is an Appointed Actuary, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.

Yes; any civil court can stay disciplinary proceedings at any time upon payment of court fees, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Yes; all disciplinary disputes must be instituted in the District Court, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 50 explicitly bars civil court jurisdiction over matters statutory authorities under the Act are empowered to decide, directing all appeals exclusively to the Appellate Authority.
explanationIncorrect: Exclusion of civil court jurisdiction prevents parallel conflicting litigation.

question: Under Section 51 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what is the effect of the Act on other laws, such as the Insurance Act 1938 or Companies Act 1956?
options: The Actuaries Act repeals all provisions of the Insurance Act 1938, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
The Actuaries Act applies only if the Companies Act does not apply, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
The provisions of the Actuaries Act 2006 shall be in addition to, and not in derogation of, the provisions of any other law for the time being in force.
The Actuaries Act is subordinate to the guidelines of individual private insurers, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Section 51 establishes that the provisions of the Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, other laws. Actuaries must comply with both the Actuaries Act and sectoral laws like the Insurance Act.
explanationIncorrect: Non-derogation ensures harmonious coexistence with the Insurance Act and Companies Act.

question: Under Section 53 of the Actuaries Act 2006, who is authorized to execute contracts, deeds, and instruments on behalf of the Council?
options: Any student actuary who has passed at least 10 exam papers, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
The manager of the nearest commercial bank branch, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
The local municipal ward councillor, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The President, or any other member or officer of the Institute authorized by the Council in that behalf.
explanationCorrect: Section 53 provides that all contracts, deeds, and instruments on behalf of the Council shall be executed by the President or authorized member/officer.
explanationIncorrect: Formal statutory execution requires authorized Council signatories.

question: Under Section 54 of the Actuaries Act 2006, who has the statutory power to remove difficulties arising in giving effect to the provisions of the Act within the first two years of its commencement?
options: The Central Government, by order published in the Official Gazette, not inconsistent with the provisions of the Act.
The President of the Institute by issuing an administrative decree, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
The Chief Justice of India by executive proclamation, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
The General Insurance Council by unanimous vote, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Section 54 grants the Central Government power to make orders to remove difficulties within two years from commencement.
explanationIncorrect: Henry VIII removal-of-difficulties clauses are vested exclusively in the Central Government.

question: Under Section 56(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, which of the following is a specific subject on which the Council is empowered to frame binding regulations?
options: Fixing mandatory life insurance claim settlement ratios for LIC, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Regulating the foreign exchange rate of the Indian Rupee, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Fixing statutory income tax brackets for all insurance company employees, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
The standard and conduct of examinations, fees for admission/examinations, terms of office of Council members, and procedures for granting/cancelling Certificates of Practice.
explanationCorrect: Section 56(2) details regulation-making powers: examinations, fees, COP procedures, Council elections, and disciplinary procedures.
explanationIncorrect: Tax brackets, forex rates, or claim ratios are outside Council regulatory powers.

question: Under Section 56(3) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what must the Central Government do with every rule and regulation made under the Act?
options: Submit them to the International Monetary Fund for ratification, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Store them in the National Archives with no public access, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Cause every rule made by Central Government and every regulation made by Council to be laid before each House of Parliament while in session for a total period of thirty days.
Publish them on Wikipedia, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 56(3) mandates parliamentary laying: every rule and regulation must be laid before each House of Parliament for 30 days for parliamentary scrutiny.
explanationIncorrect: Parliamentary oversight ensures legislative review of delegated legislation.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, First Schedule, Part I, Clause 10
question: An actuary in practice accepts an appointment as an Appointed Actuary on a contingent fee arrangement, whereby the actuary receives 2% of the insurer's reported accounting profits. Under Part I, Clause (10) of the First Schedule, how is this viewed?
options: A legitimate incentive bonus aligning interests with shareholders, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Permitted provided the percentage does not exceed 5%, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

Professional misconduct: an actuary in practice charges or offers to charge fees based on a percentage of profits or contingent upon the findings or results of such work, except as permitted by Council regulations.
Permitted if the IRDAI was informed in advance, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Clause (10), Part I of the First Schedule prohibits charging fees based on percentages of profits or contingent upon the findings or results of actuarial work.
explanationIncorrect: Contingent fee arrangements compromise actuarial objectivity and create severe conflicts of interest.

source: Actuaries Act 2006, Second Schedule, Part I, Clause 5
question: An actuary issues an actuarial certificate stating that a general insurance company's motor reserves are adequate, knowing that the company omitted 30% of its reported claims. Under Part I, Clause (5) of the Second Schedule, how is this treated?
options: A harmless commercial exaggeration, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
The actuary is immune because the management prepared the data, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Grave professional misconduct: an actuary fails to report a material misstatement known to them to appear in an actuarial report or valuation with which they are concerned in a professional capacity.
A confidential business practice protected by attorney-client privilege, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Clause (5), Part I of the Second Schedule explicitly penalizes failure to report material misstatements known to appear in actuarial reports as grave professional misconduct.
explanationIncorrect: Knowingly certifying false reports is a critical Second Schedule offense punishable by permanent expulsion.

question: Under Section 10 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what is the consequence if a person not registered as a member uses any name, title, or letters implying they are a member of the Institute?
options: They commit an offense punishable under Section 38 with a fine on first conviction and imprisonment and/or fine on subsequent conviction.
They must pay a double registration fee when eventually taking exams, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
They are barred from visiting Mumbai, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
They are automatically awarded an Honorary Fellowship, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 10 and Section 38 penalize falsely claiming membership or using unauthorized actuarial letters with criminal sanctions.
explanationIncorrect: Impersonating an actuary or misrepresenting qualifications is a punishable statutory offense.

question: Under Section 19(2)(i) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what specific duty is laid upon the Council regarding professional standards?
options: Managing the national foreign exchange reserves, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Setting the price of reinsurance retrocession contracts, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Appointing judges to the High Court, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
The framing of Actuarial Practice Standards (APS), Guidance Notes (GN), and Professional Conduct Standards (PCS) to guide members in discharge of their professional duties.
explanationCorrect: Section 19(2)(i) authorizes the Council to issue practice standards, guidance notes, and ethical codes governing members' professional conduct.
explanationIncorrect: Issuing practice standards (such as APS 9 and APS 34) is grounded in Section 19(2)(i).

question: What is the overarching public purpose of the Actuaries Act 2006 as set forth in its preamble and Parliamentary Statement of Objects and Reasons?
options: To establish a government department to nationalize all private insurance companies, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

To provide for the regulation and development of the profession of actuaries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, establishing a statutory self-regulatory Institute to protect policyholders and the public interest.

To create a closed trade union to restrict entry into the financial services sector, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
To eliminate all mathematical examinations and replace them with interviews, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: The Preamble to the Actuaries Act 2006 states: 'An Act to provide for regulating and developing the profession of Actuaries and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.'
explanationIncorrect: The Act established a statutory regulatory institute to uphold professional competence, public confidence, and policyholder protection.

question: Under Section 11 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what system of voting is mandated for the election of members to the Council?
options: Direct appointment by lottery conducted by the Honorary Secretary, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Elections shall be conducted in the prescribed manner by proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Simple first-past-the-post majority voting by show of hands, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Block voting where the candidate with the most overall votes takes all open seats, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Section 11 provides that elections to the Council shall be conducted in the prescribed manner, using proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
explanationIncorrect: Single transferable vote ensures proportional representation of diverse professional viewpoints.

question: Under Section 20(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, in which instruments is the Council permitted to invest moneys of the Fund of the Institute not immediately required for expenditure?
options: In equity shares of startup insurance brokers, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
In government securities, or in other securities approved by the Central Government, or in deposits with scheduled banks.
In real estate land development projects in offshore tax havens, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
In high-yield speculative cryptocurrency derivatives, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 20(2) permits investment of surplus funds in government securities, securities approved by the Central Government, or fixed deposits with scheduled banks.
explanationIncorrect: Speculative investments or cryptocurrencies are strictly prohibited by Section 20.

question: Under Section 28(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006 and the 2008 Disciplinary Rules, what is the standard timeframe within which the Director (Discipline) must submit the prima facie opinion to the Board of Discipline or Disciplinary Committee?
options: Within twenty-four (24) hours, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Within eighteen (18) months, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Within five (5) years, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Within sixty (60) days from the receipt of the complaint or information.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 28 and the 2008 Misconduct Rules, the Director (Discipline) is required to formulate and place the prima facie opinion within 60 days of receiving the complaint.
explanationIncorrect: The 60-day prima facie timeline ensures prompt threshold screening.

question: If the Director (Discipline) arrives at a prima facie opinion that a member is NOT guilty of any professional or other misconduct, what is the procedural outcome under Section 28?
options: The complainant is automatically sentenced to 30 days in civil prison, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
The opinion is placed before the Board of Discipline, and if the Board agrees, the complaint is closed; if the Board disagrees, it may direct further inquiry.
The member is awarded Rs. 5 Lakhs compensation by the President, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
The complaint is instantly destroyed with no record kept, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 28, a finding of 'not guilty' by the Director must still be placed before the Board of Discipline for concurrence. If the Board agrees, the matter is closed; if not, further inquiry is ordered.
explanationIncorrect: The Director cannot unilaterally dismiss a complaint without Board concurrence.

question: Under Section 32 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what action is taken when the Disciplinary Committee submits its final report finding an actuary guilty of Second Schedule misconduct?
options: The Disciplinary Committee itself affords an opportunity of hearing to the member on the proposed penalty, and passes an order imposing sanctions under Section 30(2).
The report is sent to the local police for immediate criminal arrest, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
The report is forwarded to the United Nations for international sanction, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
The Council holds a public referendum of all students to determine punishment, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 30 and 32, the Disciplinary Committee conducts the penalty hearing and issues binding orders of reprimand, removal, or fine.
explanationIncorrect: The Disciplinary Committee has statutory adjudicatory powers under Section 30(2).

question: Under Section 35 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what confidentiality obligation binds officers, members of Council, and committees regarding disciplinary matters?
options: All complaint details must be leaked to the press within 48 hours, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
No person shall disclose any information or document relating to disciplinary inquiries except to the extent necessary for carrying out duties under the Act, or in legal proceedings.
Witness testimonies must be broadcast live on commercial television, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
There is no confidentiality once a complaint is filed, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 35 imposes strict statutory confidentiality: information and documents related to inquiries cannot be disclosed except for statutory duty performance or court proceedings.
explanationIncorrect: Confidentiality protects members' reputations against frivolous or unproven allegations.

question: Under Section 43(4) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what is the term of office for the Chairperson and members of the Quality Review Board?
options: One (1) year with mandatory rotation, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Five (5) years full-time, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Ten (10) years, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Three (3) years from the date of appointment, and they are part-time members.
explanationCorrect: Section 43(4) specifies that the Chairperson and members of the QRB hold office for a term of three years and serve in a part-time capacity.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Under Section 43(4) of the Actuaries Act 2006, members of the Quality Review Board hold office for a statutory term of three years and serve on a part-time basis; alternative options cite incorrect term lengths (such as five years or lifetime appointments) or full-time executive status.

question: Under Section 44(b) of the Actuaries Act 2006, in what specific areas does the Quality Review Board review the quality of services provided by members of the Institute?
options: Review the quality of services provided by the members of the Institute including actuarial audit services.
Review the personal investment portfolios of actuaries, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Review the grammatical style of actuaries' personal emails, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Review the pricing of motor vehicles manufactured in India, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Section 44(b) explicitly mandates the QRB to 'review the quality of services provided by the members of the Institute including actuarial audit services.'
explanationIncorrect: Actuarial audit reviews ensure high-level technical and statutory compliance.

question: Under Section 46(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, upon the publication of a notification superseding the Council, where do all powers and duties of the Council vest?
options: In the High Court of Bombay, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
In such person or persons as the Central Government may appoint in that behalf, and all properties vest in the Central Government until the Council is reconstituted.
In the senior-most student actuary, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
In the Life Insurance Corporation of India, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Section 46(2) provides that upon supersession, all Council powers, duties, and properties vest in a person appointed by the Central Government until reconstitution.
explanationIncorrect: Central Government appointees administer the Institute during supersession.

question: Under Section 46(3) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what must the Central Government do before the expiration of the one-year supersession period?
options: Merge the Institute with the Institute of Company Secretaries, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Reconstitute the Council by fresh elections and nominations in accordance with Section 12.
Appoint the sitting Prime Minister as permanent President, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Abolish the actuarial profession in India permanently, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 46(3) mandates that before the period of supersession expires, the Central Government shall take steps to reconstitute the Council by fresh election and nomination.
explanationIncorrect: Democracy is restored via fresh elections before the 1-year supersession ends.

question: Under Section 52 of the Actuaries Act 2006, who is entitled to use the designation 'Actuary' in India?
options: Only an individual whose name is currently entered in the Register of Members of the Institute of Actuaries of India.
Any risk manager in a public sector undertaking, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Anyone who has completed a 3-month online certificate course in data science, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Any professor of pure mathematics, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 52 restricts the title 'Actuary' exclusively to members whose names are entered in the Institute's statutory Register.
explanationIncorrect: Using the title without statutory registration violates Section 52 and triggers Section 38 penalties.

question: Under Section 9(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what must an actuary submit when applying for the grant or annual renewal of a Certificate of Practice?
options: A character reference from three High Court judges, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
An application in the prescribed form, accompanied by the prescribed annual practice fee.
A physical gold coin deposited in the Council vault, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
A written endorsement from the CEO of an insurance company, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Section 9(2) prescribes that applications for a COP must be in the specified form accompanied by the prescribed fee.
explanationIncorrect: Statutory application and fee payment are the prerequisites under Section 9(2).

question: Under Section 9(3) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what happens to a Certificate of Practice if the member fails to pay their annual membership subscription fee?
options: The COP is automatically transferred to the member's employer.
The Certificate of Practice shall be liable to be cancelled or suspended by the Council.
The member is fined Rs. 50,000 per month, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
The COP remains valid for 10 years regardless of fee payment, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

explanationIncorrect: A valid COP is contingent on maintaining active membership standing.

question: Under Section 18 of the Actuaries Act 2006, what is the procedure for the removal of the President or Vice-President by the Council?
options: By a simple majority of 51% of members present and voting, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
The President cannot be removed under any circumstances, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
By an executive order issued by the Executive Director, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
By a resolution passed by a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total number of members of the Council at a meeting specially convened for the purpose.

explanationIncorrect: A supermajority (2/3 of total members) protects leadership from arbitrary unseating.

question: Under Section 21(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, who serves as the ex officio Chairperson of the Executive Committee of the Council?

The Director (Discipline).
The President of the Institute.
The Chairperson of the Quality Review Board.

explanationIncorrect: The President heads the Executive Committee ex officio.

question: Under Section 22(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, can a member of the Council or an officer of the Institute be appointed as the statutory auditor of the Institute?

explanationIncorrect: Auditor independence is strictly protected by statutory disqualification of insiders.

question: Under Section 28(3) of the Actuaries Act 2006, if the Director (Discipline) finds a prima facie case of misconduct falling under the First Schedule, to which body is the case referred?

To the Disciplinary Committee.
To the Quality Review Board.
Directly to the Supreme Court of India.

explanationIncorrect: The Board of Discipline handles First Schedule offenses.

question: Under Section 28(4) of the Actuaries Act 2006, if the Director (Discipline) finds a prima facie case of misconduct falling under the Second Schedule or both the First and Second Schedules, to which body is the case referred?

To the local police commissioner.
To the Board of Discipline.
To the Disciplinary Committee.
explanationCorrect: Section 28(4) mandates that Second Schedule misconduct (or combined First and Second Schedule offenses) must be referred to the Disciplinary Committee.
explanationIncorrect: The 5-member Disciplinary Committee handles grave Second Schedule misconduct.

question: Under Section 36(2) of the Actuaries Act 2006, what powers does the Appellate Authority possess when disposing of an appeal filed by an actuary?
options: It must refer every appeal to the President of India, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
It can only approve the order without any power of modification, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
The Appellate Authority may confirm, modify or set aside the order, impose any penalty or set aside, reduce, or enhance the penalty, or remit the case for fresh inquiry.
It can sentence the actuary to life imprisonment, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 36(2) grants full appellate powers: confirm, modify, set aside, enhance/reduce penalty, or remit for fresh inquiry.
explanationIncorrect: The Appellate Authority exercises comprehensive appellate jurisdiction.

question: Under Section 38(3) of the Actuaries Act 2006, if a fine imposed by a court under Section 38 is not paid, how is it recovered?

It shall be recovered as if it were an arrear of land revenue under the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973.
explanationCorrect: Section 38(3) provides that unpaid fines shall be recovered in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure as arrears of land revenue.
explanationIncorrect: Recovery as arrears of land revenue enables state attachment and distress warrant procedures.

question: Under Section 47 of the Actuaries Act 2006, who bears the expenses incurred by the Quality Review Board, and out of which fund are they paid?

QRB members must pay their own travel and office expenses, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
All expenses incurred by the Quality Review Board are borne by the Institute and paid out of the Fund of the Institute.
Expenses are paid out of the Prime Minister's Discretionary Relief Fund, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.

explanationIncorrect: The Institute finances the QRB from the statutory Fund.

options: There is no daily cap; an actuary can complete 50 CPD hours in a single 24-hour day, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Strict conversion: <0.5h=0; 0.5-<1.5h=1; 1.5-<2.5h=2; 2.5-<3.5h=3; 3.5-<4.5h=4; 4.5-<5.5h=5; >=5.5h=6 hours max per single calendar day (excluding meals).
Attending a 10-hour seminar awards 24 CPD hours in a single day, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Every 10 minutes of webinar watching awards 5 CPD hours, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Strict conversion: <0.5h=0; 0.5-<1.5h=1; 1.5-<2.5h=2; 2.5-<3.5h=3; 3.5-<4.5h=4; 4.5-<5.5h=5; >=5.5h=6 hours max per single calendar day (excluding meals).
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), a practitioner logging peer review discussions as professional development, how does Self-Attestation Deadline (31st May) apply?
options: Annual online self-attestation must be submitted on the IAI portal by 31st May (within 2 months of compliance year ending 31st March).
Self-attestation deadline is 31st December of the following decade, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Attestation must be submitted in person at the President's private residence, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
There is no attestation requirement; the Institute monitors brainwaves, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Annual online self-attestation must be submitted on the IAI portal by 31st May (within 2 months of compliance year ending 31st March).
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), a practitioner logging peer review discussions as professional development, how does 5-Year CPD Record Retention Mandate apply?
options: Members must preserve original attendance certificates, syllabus notes, and verifiable CPD evidence for at least 5 years (e.g. FY 2020-21 kept until FY 2025-26).
Records must be chiseled on stone tablets and buried in the ground, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Records must be permanently deleted immediately after online attestation, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Records need to be retained for exactly 3 days, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Members must preserve original attendance certificates, syllabus notes, and verifiable CPD evidence for at least 5 years (e.g. FY 2020-21 kept until FY 2025-26).
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), a practitioner logging peer review discussions as professional development, how does Public Website Listing of Defaulters (1st July) apply?
options: Defaulters are forced to teach elementary school algebra, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Names of non-compliant members are publicly posted on the IAI website on 1st July each year; repeat defaults lead to COP revocation and disciplinary action.
Defaulters are sent on all-expenses-paid luxury vacations to Europe, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Names of defaulters are kept strictly secret and erased from all databases, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Names of non-compliant members are publicly posted on the IAI website on 1st July each year; repeat defaults lead to COP revocation and disciplinary action.
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), a practitioner logging peer review discussions as professional development, how does Verifiable Learning Criteria vs Informal Reading apply?
options: Watching fictional Hollywood movies about math counts as professional ethics CPD, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

Reading casual financial news headlines on a mobile phone counts as verifiable technical CPD, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Verifiable learning requires organized curriculum, proof of attendance, certificates, or verified logs; informal private magazine reading does NOT count.
Verifiable CPD can only be completed in an airplane flying at 30,000 feet, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Verifiable learning requires organized curriculum, proof of attendance, certificates, or verified logs; informal private magazine reading does NOT count.
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), an actuary logging training on newly enacted Ind AS 117 accounting standards, how does Category 1 COP Holder Mandatory Hours (24 Hours) apply?
options: Must complete 500 hours annually including mandatory physical fitness drills, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Must complete minimum 24 verifiable CPD hours per year: at least 15 technical in primary practice area, at least 6 professional/ethical, max 3 other.
CPD is optional for COP holders; only students must complete hours, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Must complete 100 hours of technical coding without any ethics training, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Must complete minimum 24 verifiable CPD hours per year: at least 15 technical in primary practice area, at least 6 professional/ethical, max 3 other.
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), an actuary logging training on newly enacted Ind AS 117 accounting standards, how does Additional Practice Area Rule (+8 Hours per Extra Area) apply?
options: Any COP holder practicing in more than one area must complete an additional 8 verifiable technical CPD hours for EACH additional practice area.

The actuary must take a 1-year sabbatical before entering an additional practice area, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Practicing in additional areas reduces total CPD requirement by 50%, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

Additional practice areas require zero extra hours if the actuary is over 50 years old, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Any COP holder practicing in more than one area must complete an additional 8 verifiable technical CPD hours for EACH additional practice area.
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), an actuary logging training on newly enacted Ind AS 117 accounting standards, how does Category 2 Active Fellow without COP (15 Hours) apply?
options: Must complete minimum 15 verifiable CPD hours per year (at least 9 technical, at least 3 professional/ethical, max 3 other).
Must complete 50 hours of physical community service in a public park, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Exempt from all professional learning requirements for life, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Must complete exactly 1 hour of CPD every decade, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Must complete minimum 15 verifiable CPD hours per year (at least 9 technical, at least 3 professional/ethical, max 3 other).
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), an actuary logging training on newly enacted Ind AS 117 accounting standards, how does Mutual Recognition Exemption for Category 2 Fellows apply?
options: Foreign bodies must send their President to Mumbai to sign an exemption deed, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Exemption requires paying a cash fee of Rs. 1 Lakh to the Ministry of Finance, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

Foreign CPD compliance is illegal in India and results in immediate COP cancellation, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Category 2 Fellows compliant with CPD requirements of a recognized overseas actuarial body (IFoA, SOA, CAS) are fully exempt upon submitting proof.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Category 2 Fellows compliant with CPD requirements of a recognized overseas actuarial body (IFoA, SOA, CAS) are fully exempt upon submitting proof.
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9: Continuing Professional Development v4.00), an actuary logging training on newly enacted Ind AS 117 accounting standards, how does Category 3 Inactive / Retired Fellows (Exemption) apply?
options: Retired Fellows can continue signing statutory life insurance balance sheets without CPD, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Members fully retired from actuarial work can apply in writing at least 3 months prior to year-end for Category 3 inactive status; exempt from annual CPD.
Category 3 status is granted automatically without written application, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Inactive Fellows must surrender their Fellowship title and academic degrees, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under APS 9 (v4.00), the mandatory requirement is: Members fully retired from actuarial work can apply in writing at least 3 months prior to year-end for Category 3 inactive status; exempt from annual CPD.
explanationIncorrect: The competing options violate specific hour thresholds, conversion brackets, retention mandates, or deadline rules of APS 9.

question: Under which specific statutory provision of the Actuaries Act, 2006 does the Council of the Institute of Actuaries of India derive its legal authority to issue and enforce Actuarial Practice Standard 9 (APS 9 v4.00)?
options: Section 19(2)(i) of the Actuaries Act, 2006.
Section 43 of the Actuaries Act, 2006.
Section 21(1) of the Actuaries Act, 2006.
Section 9(1) of the Actuaries Act, 2006.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 1 of APS 9 (v4.00), the standard is issued by the Council in exercise of powers vested under Section 19(2)(i) of the Actuaries Act, 2006.
explanationIncorrect: Section 9 deals with Certificates of Practice. Section 21 deals with statutory committees. Section 43 deals with the Quality Review Board.

question: When was APS 9 (Version 4.00) formally approved by the Council of the Institute of Actuaries of India, and from which CPD compliance year did it become mandatory?
options: Approved by Council on 19th June 2021; mandatory from CPD year 2021-22.
Approved by Council on 21st July 2018; mandatory from CPD year 2018-19.
Approved by Council on 28th March 2015; mandatory from CPD year 2015-16.
Approved by Council on 8th October 2021; mandatory from CPD year 2022-23.
explanationCorrect: Under the Status section and President's notification of APS 9 (v4.00), the Council approved Version 4.00 on 19th June 2021, and it became mandatory starting from the CPD year 2021-22.
explanationIncorrect: Version 3.00 was approved on 21/07/2018. Version 2.00 was approved in March 2015. 8th October 2021 was the circular circulation date.

question: Under APS 9 (v4.00) Section 4.2.1, how is a 'Category 1' member defined, and what is their core compliance trigger?
options: All Fellow members actively employed in life or general insurance companies regardless of whether they hold a CoP.
All Fellow members who serve as appointed actuaries or statutory signing actuaries only.
All members who have completed more than 10 years of post-qualification actuarial experience.
All active Fellow members who hold or apply for a Certificate of Practice (CoP) under Section 9 of the Actuaries Act 2006.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 4.2.1 of APS 9 (v4.00), Category 1 encompasses all active Fellow members who hold or apply for a Certificate of Practice (CoP).
explanationIncorrect: Category 2 applies to active Fellows without a CoP. Employment sector or years of experience do not define Category 1.

question: A Fellow of the Institute working in a global analytics consultancy does not hold a Certificate of Practice (CoP) but performs actuarial modelling and pricing for overseas clients. Under APS 9 (v4.00), which membership category applies to this member?
options: Category 4: Because the client base is entirely outside the territorial jurisdiction of India, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Category 1: Because the consulting work involves pricing and commercial modelling, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Category 2: Active Fellow member who does not hold a CoP and undertakes paid or unpaid work relying on actuarial training and experience.

Category 3: Because the member does not sign statutory actuarial certificates in India, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.2.2 defines Category 2 as all active Fellow members who do not hold a CoP and who undertake paid or unpaid work which relies upon their actuarial training and experience.
explanationIncorrect: Category 1 requires holding or applying for a CoP. Category 3 and 4 apply strictly to inactive members.
