question: An actuary who qualified as a Fellow of the Institute of Actuaries of India in November 2023 plans their CPD obligations. Under Section 10.3 of APS 9 (v4.00), when do mandatory CPD requirements first become applicable to this newly qualified Fellow?
options: From the next CPD year (i.e., starting 1st April 2024).
Immediately on a pro-rata basis for the remaining months of the 2023-24 CPD year.
Only after they complete their first two years of continuous post-Fellowship work experience.
Exactly 12 calendar months after the date of receiving the Fellowship admission letter.
explanationCorrect: Section 10.3 explicitly states: 'For newly qualified members, the CPD requirements will be applicable from next CPD year.'
explanationIncorrect: APS 9 does not impose pro-rata CPD or delayed 12-month/2-year grace periods on newly qualified members; compliance begins from the next CPD year.

question: Under Section 4.3 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the statutory definition of the 'CPD year' for all Fellow members of the Institute?
options: A period of one year commencing from 1st April and ending on 31st March.
A calendar year commencing from 1st January and ending on 31st December.
A period of 12 months running from the anniversary of the member's admission as a Fellow.
A period of 12 months aligned with the member's annual birth month.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.3 states: 'The CPD year(s) for all Fellow members of the Institute shall be a period of one year (from 1st April to 31st March).'
explanationIncorrect: The Indian actuarial CPD year strictly follows the financial year (1st April to 31st March), not calendar years or individual membership anniversaries.

question: A Fellow holding a Certificate of Practice (Category 1) is planning their annual CPD portfolio for FY 2024-25 in the Life Insurance practice area. What is the mandatory minimum breakdown of their 24 CPD hours under Section 4.4.3?
options: Minimum 15 hours pre-approved verifiable technical CPD in Life Insurance, minimum 6 hours pre-approved verifiable professional CPD, and maximum 3 hours other verifiable CPD.

Minimum 20 hours technical CPD and minimum 4 hours professional conduct CPD, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

Minimum 12 hours technical CPD, minimum 6 hours professional CPD, and minimum 6 hours business management CPD, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.

Minimum 18 hours technical CPD and minimum 6 hours professional CPD, with zero allowance for other verifiable hours, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 4.4.3, a Category 1 member requires 24 CPD hours annually: (1) Minimum 15 pre-approved verifiable technical CPD hours in specific practice area; (2) Minimum 6 pre-approved verifiable professional CPD hours; (3) Maximum 3 hours other verifiable CPD.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Section 4.4.3 mandates a strict portfolio breakdown of at least 15 technical pre-approved hours, at least 6 professional hours, and up to 3 other hours. Alternative options distort this statutory allocation.

question: Under Section 4.5 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the exact mandatory minimum annual CPD requirement and composition for Category 2 active Fellows who do not hold a CoP?
options: Minimum 10 CPD hours per year: 5 technical hours and 5 professional hours, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Minimum 15 CPD hours per year: at least 9 pre-approved verifiable technical hours, at least 3 pre-approved verifiable professional hours, and maximum 3 other verifiable hours.
Minimum 24 CPD hours per year: identical to Category 1 members, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Minimum 12 CPD hours per year: 8 technical hours and 4 professional hours, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.5 prescribes: for active Fellows without CoP, minimum 15 CPD hours each year, of which (i) minimum 9 hours pre-approved verifiable technical, (ii) minimum 3 hours pre-approved verifiable professional, and (iii) maximum 3 hours other verifiable.
explanationIncorrect: 24 hours applies to Category 1 CoP holders. 10 and 12 hours are incorrect figures.

question: An Appointed Actuary of a composite reinsurer holds a CoP in Life Insurance and also signs statutory valuations in Health Insurance. Under Section 5 (Situation 2) of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the total minimum technical CPD requirement?
options: 24 technical CPD hours: total hours remain capped at 24 regardless of practice areas.
15 technical CPD hours: because Life Insurance encompasses Health Insurance technical topics.
23 technical CPD hours: 15 hours in Life Insurance plus an additional 8 hours in Health Insurance.
30 technical CPD hours: 15 hours in Life Insurance and 15 hours in Health Insurance.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 5 (Situation 2), if a member practices in multiple areas, the required minimum technical CPD hours increases by 8 CPD hours for each additional area of practice (15 + 8 = 23 technical hours).
explanationIncorrect: Wrongly duplicates the full 15 hours. Ignores the mandatory multi-practice surcharge. Confusing total minimum baseline with technical requirements.

question: A senior consulting actuary holds a Certificate of Practice covering three distinct practice areas: General Insurance, Health Insurance, and Pensions & Other Employee Benefits. Under APS 9 (v4.00), what is the actuary's minimum annual technical CPD requirement?
options: 31 technical CPD hours (15 hours for the primary practice area + 8 hours + 8 hours for the two additional areas).
23 technical CPD hours (the 8-hour surcharge applies only once regardless of the number of additional areas).
24 technical CPD hours (capped by the total annual CoP requirement), provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
45 technical CPD hours (15 hours for each of the three practice areas), on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 5, the technical requirement increases by 8 hours under EACH additional area of practice. For 1 primary + 2 additional areas, technical hours = 15 + 8 + 8 = 31 hours.
explanationIncorrect: Assumes full 15h per area. Ignores Section 5. Fails to apply the +8h rule per additional area.

question: Which of the following lists correctly represents the official recognized areas of actuarial practice enumerated in Section 5 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: a) Life Insurance; b) Non-Life Insurance; c) Reinsurance; d) Banking; e) Enterprise Risk Management, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

a) Statutory Valuation; b) Product Pricing; c) Solvency II; d) Asset-Liability Management; e) Data Science, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.

a) Life Insurance; b) General Insurance; c) Health Insurance; d) Social Security; e) Microinsurance, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
a) Life Insurance; b) Health Insurance; c) General Insurance; d) Pension and Other Employee Benefits; e) Finance, Investments and Management; and f) any other area decided by Council.
explanationCorrect: Section 5 of APS 9 explicitly enumerates: 'a) Life Insurance; b) Health Insurance; c) General Insurance; d) Pension and Other Employee Benefits, e) Finance, Investments and Management and f) any other area as decided by the Council from time to time.'
explanationIncorrect: Other options list functional sub-disciplines or informal classifications rather than the statutory six practice categories of Section 5.

question: An actuary applies for a new Certificate of Practice (CoP) or restoration of an expired CoP in October 2024 but did not complete the required 24 CPD hours during FY 2023-24. How does Section 4.4.2 treat CPD hours earned during the year of application (FY 2024-25)?
options: Hours earned during FY 2024-25 may be double-counted for both initial issuance and the subsequent FY 2025-26 renewal.
The application must be summarily rejected because hours must strictly be earned in the preceding full financial year.
Hours earned during FY 2024-25 may be counted towards the initial issuance/restoration, but CANNOT be counted again for renewal of the CoP for FY 2025-26.

The member is granted an unconditional one-year waiver from all CPD requirements upon paying a double fee, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 4.4.2, CPD hours earned during the year of application/restoration may be counted for total CPD hours for that issuance, but 'these CPD hours will not be used/counted for renewal of CoP for next year.'
explanationIncorrect: Permits prohibited double-counting. Ignores the safe-harbour mechanism of Section 4.4.2. Alternative options  fictitious.

question: On what date is the eligibility of a Fellow member for the annual renewal of their Certificate of Practice reviewed by the Institute under Section 4.4.1 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: On 1st July every year, concurrent with the publication of the defaulters list, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
On the individual birth date of the practicing Fellow, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
On 31st December every year, based on the preceding calendar year, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
With effect from 1st April every year, based on the full CPD year(s) immediately prior to the CPD year to which the CoP applies.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.4.1 specifies: 'The eligibility for COPs as per the COP Guidelines will be reviewed with effect from 1st April every year and eligibility with respect to CPD activities will be based on the full CPD year/s immediately prior...'
explanationIncorrect: The review date is strictly 1st April based on the prior full financial year.

question: A Fellow member holding a CoP accumulates 15 hours of technical CPD in General Insurance, 6 hours of professional CPD, and 5 hours of other verifiable CPD during FY 2024-25. How many total CPD hours can the member count toward their 24-hour requirement under Section 4.4.3?
options: 21 hours, because exceeding the cap on other CPD invalidates the entire other category.
23 hours, because other CPD is discounted by 50% under Council guidelines.
26 hours, because all verifiable hours are counted without restriction, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
24 hours, because other verifiable CPD hours are subject to a strict maximum cap of 3 hours (15 + 6 + 3 = 24).
explanationCorrect: Section 4.4.3(3) provides: 'A maximum of 3 CPD hours may be earned as other verifiable CPD hours.' Excess hours beyond 3 cannot be credited toward the 24-hour mandatory minimum.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Section 4.4.3 mandates a strict portfolio breakdown of at least 15 technical pre-approved hours, at least 6 professional hours, and up to 3 other hours. Alternative options distort this statutory allocation.

question: Under Section 4.4.3 of APS 9 (v4.00), can a Category 1 CoP holder satisfy their 3-hour non-core CPD requirement with additional pre-approved technical or professional hours instead of 'other verifiable' hours?
options: Yes, but only if the additional hours are in professional conduct, not technical subjects, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
No; exceeding 15 technical hours requires Council permission, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
No; exactly 3 hours must be drawn from informal self-study or employer training under 'other verifiable' hours.
Yes; any other pre-approved CPD credits, irrespective of whether technical or professional, can be used to satisfy the 3-hour balance.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 5 (Situation 1) and Section 4.4.3, '3 hrs may be earned as other verifiable CPD hours or any other pre-approved CPD credits irrespective whether its Professional / Technical.'
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Section 4.4.3 mandates a strict portfolio breakdown of at least 15 technical pre-approved hours, at least 6 professional hours, and up to 3 other hours. Alternative options distort this statutory allocation.

question: A Fellow member holding a CoP in Pensions decides not to renew their CoP for the upcoming financial year. Under Section 11.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the default assumption regarding their CPD obligations?
options: The member must continue fulfilling Category 1 (24 hours) CPD for a 2-year run-off period, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

The member is automatically classified as Category 4 and struck off the Institute register, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
The member is granted a permanent 3-year CPD holiday, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
It will be assumed that the member should meet the CPD requirements of Category 2 (or any other applicable category), subject to prior intimation through email.
explanationCorrect: Section 11.2 states: 'If Category 1 member does not wish to renew his CoP, it would be assumed that he / she should meet the CPD requirements of Category 2 or any other category as the case may be with prior intimation through email.'
explanationIncorrect: Non-renewal of CoP reverts the active actuary to Category 2 (15 hours) CPD requirements.

question: What is the core distinction between 'Technical CPD hours' and 'Professional CPD hours' as defined under Section 6 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: Technical CPD involves mathematical calculations, whereas Professional CPD involves attending commercial vendor conferences.
Technical CPD requires written examinations, whereas Professional CPD requires only signing an attendance sheet.
Technical CPD enhances knowledge in a specific practice area, whereas Professional CPD enhances understanding of professional obligations and expected conduct.

Technical CPD is organized exclusively by the IAI, whereas Professional CPD is organized by overseas bodies, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Sections 6.1 and 6.2 define: Technical CPD means time spent acquiring knowledge enhancing each specific practice area; Professional CPD means time spent acquiring knowledge directly relevant to enhancing understanding of professional obligations and behaviour.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Alternative choices confuse technical practice skills with ethical/professional competencies or misstate Section 6 classifications.

question: Who has the statutory authority to designate an IAI-organised event as 'technical' or 'professional' and specify the applicable practice area under Section 6.3 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: The employer of the majority of attending delegates, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
The Council or the Committee authorized by it, designated at the time of announcement of the activity.
The individual speaker delivering the lecture at the conclusion of the session.
Each attending member based on their subjective personal learning log, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 6.3 mandates: 'For pre-approved verifiable CPD programs/events organised by the Institute, the Council or Committee authorized by it shall designate the program or event as "technical" or "professional" at the time of announcement...'
explanationIncorrect: The classification of IAI events is determined ex-ante by Council/Committee, not ex-post by speakers or attendees.

question: How are CPD hours classified when an actuary undertakes an activity that is NOT pre-approved by the Institute but qualifies under 'other verifiable CPD' (Section 6.5)?
options: The member must petition the Disciplinary Committee for retroactive classification, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Members may classify the hours as 'technical' (with practice area) or 'professional' based on their own professional judgment regarding the nature of the activity.
The activity cannot be classified into any category and yields zero CPD credit, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.

The activity must be automatically classified as 100% professional conduct regardless of content, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Section 6.5 states: 'For other verifiable CPD activities, members may classify their CPD hours as "technical" with area of practice or "professional" based on their own judgement with respect to the nature of the activity undertaken.'
explanationIncorrect: For non-pre-approved verifiable activities, members apply their own professional judgment to classify the subject matter.

question: Under Section 7.1 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the legal nature of the Institute's authority regarding the list of pre-approved verifiable CPD activities?
options: Any member can compel the inclusion of an event by submitting a formal legal requisition, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

The list is fixed permanently in the Actuaries Act and cannot be modified without Parliamentary approval, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.

The list must be ratified annually by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI), subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The Council or authorized Committee has sole discretion to add, delete, or modify eligibility, and the decision is the sole prerogative of the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Section 7.1 and 7.2.6 establish that the Council/Committee at its sole discretion may add, delete, or change eligibility; the decision is the sole prerogative of the Institute and cannot be challenged.
explanationIncorrect: IRDAI does not approve the IAI CPD list, nor is Parliamentary amendment required.

question: An external organisation wishes to have its international seminar series included in the IAI's pre-approved verifiable CPD list. Under Section 7.2.1 of APS 9, what organisational criterion must be satisfied?
options: The organising body must be an organisation of appropriate reputation in actuarial work (e.g., professional body, regulator, IAA partner body, industry group, or reputed employer).

The organising body must pay 50% of delegate registration fees to the IAI Pension Fund, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

The organising body must be incorporated as a Section 8 non-profit company under the Indian Companies Act 2013, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

The organising body must have at least three Fellows of the IAI on its Board of Directors, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Section 7.2.1 requires: 'The organising body is an organisation of appropriate reputation in the context of actuarial work, for example a professional body, a regulator, another member body/partner of the International Actuarial Association (IAA), an appropriate industry group...'
explanationIncorrect: Section 8 incorporation, IAI directors, or fee-sharing are not criteria under Section 7.2.1.

question: A boutique consulting firm organizes an invitation-only round-table on algorithmic trading reserved exclusively for its C-suite clients and partners. Can this event be included in the IAI's pre-approved verifiable CPD list under Section 7.2.2?
options: No; participation must be open for all Fellow members of the Institute and not limited to a restricted set of individuals by invitation only.

Yes; provided the technical depth is certified by a Fellow with at least 15 years experience, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
No; unless the event is held at the IAI headquarters in Navi Mumbai, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Yes; but only for the partners who delivered presentations, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 7.2.2 strictly mandates: 'Participation is open for all Fellow members of the Institute and not limited to a certain set of individuals, for example by invitation only or any other eligibility criteria.'
explanationIncorrect: Closed or invitation-only events cannot be granted pre-approved verifiable CPD status.

question: Under Section 7.2.3 of APS 9 (v4.00), what structural interaction requirement must an event meet to qualify for pre-approved verifiable CPD status?
options: The sessions must be chaired by a current sitting Council member, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Participation must expose members to an exchange of viewpoints including individuals from outside of the member's own organisation.
Every delegate must ask at least two verbal questions during the plenary session, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The event must be conducted in hybrid mode with live streaming on YouTube, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 7.2.3 requires: 'Participation exposes members to an exchange of viewpoints including individuals from outside of the member's own organisation.'
explanationIncorrect: Internal closed-shop discussions do not meet the standard for pre-approved external verifiable status.

question: How many specific informational items must an applicant submit to the Institute when applying for inclusion of an event in the pre-approved CPD list under Section 7.2.5 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: Exactly 10 minimum items (including description, organising body, hours, classification rationale, frequency, participation nature, learning outcomes, overseas recognition, evidence method, supporting materials).
Exactly 3 items (title, dates, and speaker CVs), on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Exactly 5 items (brochure, invoice, attendee list, presentation slides, and feedback forms), provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

Exactly 7 items aligned with the seven core principles of the Professional Conduct Standards, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Section 7.2.5 enumerates 10 distinct informational requirements (items 1 through 10) that must be submitted to the Institute for consideration.
explanationIncorrect: Other numbers are incorrect; Section 7.2.5 specifically lists 10 required items.

question: If the Council or Committee authorized by Council rejects an actuary's application to include an international seminar in the pre-approved CPD list, what recourse is available under Section 7.2.6?
options: The decision is the sole prerogative of the Institute and may not be challenged by any member.
The rejection is automatically stayed if five Fellows cosign a letter of protest.
The member may appeal within 30 days to the Appellate Authority under Section 36 of the Actuaries Act.
The member may demand arbitration under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996.
explanationCorrect: Section 7.2.6 explicitly provides: 'The decision for inclusion or otherwise of any activity in the pre-approved list is the sole prerogative of the Institute and may not be challenged by any member.'
explanationIncorrect: Appeals to the Appellate Authority apply to disciplinary orders, not administrative CPD pre-approval decisions.

question: An actuary spends 20 hours reading published international actuarial journals and studying textbooks at home. Under Section 8.1 of APS 9 (v4.00), how are such informal self-study activities treated?
options: They are completely disallowed and cannot be mentioned anywhere in the member's annual records, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

They can be converted to 10 technical CPD hours upon submitting a 500-word essay to the President, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
They fall under 'Other verifiable CPD hours' (provided learning can be evidenced in writing), but count toward the annual requirement up to a maximum cap of 3 hours.
They qualify as pre-approved technical CPD hours without any cap, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 8.1 and Section 4.4.3/4.5, informal self-study falls under 'Other verifiable CPD hours' and is subject to a strict cap of 3 CPD hours per year, provided demonstrable enhancement and written evidence exist.
explanationIncorrect: Self-study is never pre-approved, nor is it completely prohibitedΓÇöit is capped at 3 hours.

question: An insurer conducts an internal 2-day technical workshop for its in-house actuarial team on Ind AS 117 cash-flow modelling. Under Section 8 of APS 9 (v4.00), can the attending Fellows claim this as CPD?
options: Yes; internal training and development programs of a member's own organisation can be claimed under 'Other verifiable CPD hours' up to the 3-hour cap, provided knowledge enhancement and written evidence exist.
Yes; but only if external auditors were present in the room during the entire workshop, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Yes; it qualifies as pre-approved technical CPD for the full 12 hours attended, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

No; internal training conducted by an employer is strictly prohibited from being claimed as any form of CPD, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 8.1 expressly includes 'attending internal training and development programs of a member's own organisation' under Other Verifiable CPD, subject to Section 8.2 criteria and the 3-hour cap.
explanationIncorrect: Internal employer training is not pre-approved (as it lacks outside viewpoints and open access), but is eligible under the 3-hour other verifiable category.

question: Under Section 8.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), what two cumulative conditions must be satisfied for an activity to qualify under 'Other verifiable CPD hours'?
options: 1) The employer must issue a notarised stamp; and 2) Two Fellows must countersign the timesheet, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

1) The session must last at least 4 hours; and 2) An exam must be administered with a 70% passing grade, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
1) Demonstrable enhancement of knowledge/skills relevant to the role or actuarial personal development; and 2) Engagements and learning outcomes are capable of being evidenced in writing.

1) Prior written approval must be obtained from the Council; and 2) An application fee of Rs. 5,000 must be paid, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Section 8.2.1 and 8.2.2 require: (1) demonstrable enhancement of knowledge/skills relevant to role or personal development; and (2) engagement and learning outcomes capable of being evidenced to the Institute in writing.
explanationIncorrect: Exam passes, application fees, or notary stamps are not requirements of Section 8.2.

question: An actuary claims 3 hours of 'Other verifiable CPD' for reading regulatory circulars on their personal tablet. When audited, the actuary states they made mental notes but have no notes, logs, or written evidence. Under Section 8.2.2, is this acceptable?
options: Yes; an actuary's verbal self-declaration is conclusive evidence under the Professional Conduct Standards, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Yes; provided the actuary can show browser history logs on their tablet, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
No; because regulatory circulars can never be claimed as CPD under any circumstances, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
No; Section 8.2.2 strictly mandates that engagements in the activity as well as learning outcomes must be capable of being evidenced to the Institute in writing.
explanationCorrect: Section 8.2.2 requires that learning outcomes and engagement must be capable of being evidenced in writing. Without written documentation or learning notes, the claim fails audit validation.
explanationIncorrect: Verbal self-declaration alone does not meet the standard of written evidence under Section 8.2.2.

question: Under Section 9.1 of APS 9 (v4.00), what fundamental principle governs how an actuary determines the number of CPD hours to claim from an event?
options: Hours should only be claimed to the extent the member considers that the activity has enhanced knowledge/skills, based on self-assessment of learning outcomes (subject to daily caps).

The member must divide the attendance hours equally between technical and professional conduct, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

The member must claim exactly the total elapsed wall-clock time from arrival to departure, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

The member must claim whatever number of hours is printed on the commercial marketing brochure, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Section 9.1 provides that CPD hours should only be claimed commensurate with the member's assessment of own learning outcomes and relevance, subject to the maximum daily caps in Section 9.2.
explanationIncorrect: Claiming elapsed wall-clock time or marketing brochure estimates without reflecting actual learning violates Section 9.1.

question: An actuary attends a technical lecture that starts at 10:00 AM and concludes at 10:25 AM (25 minutes elapsed). Under the daily calculation table in Section 9.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), how many CPD hours can be claimed?
options: 0.4 CPD hours proportional to the minutes attended.
0.5 CPD hours rounded to the nearest half hour.
1.0 CPD hour under the minimum session allowance.
Zero CPD hours, because time spent < 0.5 hours yields zero credit.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9.2 table: '< 0.5 hrs' spent yields 'Zero CPD hour'. Sessions under 30 minutes yield no credit.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: An actuary attends a virtual seminar on climate risk for exactly 50 minutes (0.83 hours). Under Section 9.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the allowable CPD credit?
options: 0.83 CPD hours recorded down to the exact hundredth.
One CPD hour (time spent >= 0.5 hrs and < 1.5 hrs).
Zero CPD hours, because it did not reach a full 60 minutes.
Two CPD hours if the speaker was an international expert.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9.2 table: '>= 0.5 hrs < 1.5 hrs' yields 'One CPD hour'. 50 minutes (0.83 hrs) falls squarely into this bracket.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: A conference session on IFRS 17 runs from 2:00 PM to 3:45 PM without breaks (1 hour 45 minutes = 1.75 hours). Under the Section 9.2 conversion scale, how many CPD hours are awarded?
options: 1.75 CPD hours, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Two CPD hours (time spent >= 1.5 hrs and < 2.5 hrs).
One CPD hour, rounded down to the completed hour.
Three CPD hours, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9.2 table: '>= 1.5 hrs < 2.5 hrs' yields 'Two CPD hours'. 1.75 hours falls in this range.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: An actuary participates in an executive workshop running continuously for 2 hours and 35 minutes (2.58 hours). Under Section 9.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), how many CPD hours are earned?
options: Four CPD hours, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Two CPD hours, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
2.5 CPD hours, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Three CPD hours (time spent >= 2.5 hrs and < 3.5 hrs).
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9.2: '>= 2.5 hrs < 3.5 hrs' yields 'Three CPD hours'. 2 hours 35 minutes is 2.58 hours.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: A full-day actuarial symposium runs from 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM (8 total elapsed hours). The schedule includes a 1-hour lunch break, a 30-minute morning tea break, and a 30-minute afternoon tea break. Under Section 9.2, how many CPD hours can be claimed?
options: Six CPD hours, because net instructional time is 6.0 hours (8.0 - 2.0 = 6.0 hrs >= 5.5 hrs), hitting the maximum daily cap of 6 hours.
Seven CPD hours, because tea breaks count as informal networking, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Five CPD hours, because full-day events are discounted by 20% for fatigue, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Eight CPD hours corresponding to the entire elapsed time from 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Net instructional time is 8 - 1 (lunch) - 1 (tea breaks) = 6.0 hours. Under Section 9.2: '>= 5.5 hrs' yields 'Six CPD hours' (the maximum daily limit). Furthermore, the Note explicitly excludes lunch breaks.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: An actuary attends a marathon 10-hour hackathon on predictive machine learning on a Saturday, working for 9.0 instructional hours (excluding lunch). Under Section 9.2, how many CPD hours can the actuary record for that calendar day?
options: Nine CPD hours, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Ten CPD hours, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Exactly 6 CPD hours, as 6 hours is the absolute maximum daily credit allowed under APS 9 (>= 5.5 hrs).
Twelve CPD hours, because weekend events carry a 1.5x multiplier, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9.2 table, any duration of '>= 5.5 hrs' yields 'Six CPD hours'. No matter how many hours are spent in a single day beyond 5.5 hours, the daily credit is capped at 6.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: An actuary attends two separate events on the same calendar day: a 2-hour morning webinar (>=1.5h <2.5h = 2 CPD hours) and a 3-hour afternoon seminar (>=2.5h <3.5h = 3 CPD hours). Under Section 9.2, what is the actuary's total CPD credit for the day?
options: 7 CPD hours, by adding arbitrary preparation time, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
5 CPD hours, because total instructional time is 5.0 hours (falling in the >= 4.5 hrs < 5.5 hrs band = 5 hours).
6 CPD hours, by rounding up each individual session, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
2 CPD hours, because only one event per day may be claimed, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 9.2 provides for 'Details calculation for CPD per day'. The total daily instructional time is 2 + 3 = 5 hours, which falls in the bracket '>= 4.5 hrs < 5.5 hrs' yielding 5 CPD hours.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: An actuary registers for a 3-day actuarial masterclass running 7 hours of instruction each day (total 21 instructional hours across 3 days). What is the maximum total CPD credit that can be claimed across the 3 days under Section 9.2?
options: 15 CPD hours (the maximum technical requirement).
21 CPD hours (matching total clock hours).
18 CPD hours (6 CPD hours maximum per day x 3 days).
24 CPD hours (the entire annual requirement in one masterclass).
explanationCorrect: Because each day exceeds 5.5 hours of instructional time, each day yields the maximum daily cap of 6 CPD hours. For 3 distinct calendar days, total credit = 6 x 3 = 18 CPD hours.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: Under the Note in Section 9.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), which of the following is explicitly excluded when computing time spent for daily CPD credit?
options: Lunch breaks.
Case-study breakout exercises conducted in teams.
Panel discussions featuring external industry experts.
Q&A sessions with the speaker at the end of the presentation.
explanationCorrect: Section 9.2 contains the explicit note: 'Note:- This excludes lunch break'. Meal times cannot be counted as instructional CPD time.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: An actuary attends an online webinar running from 6:00 PM to 9:15 PM (3 hours 15 minutes = 3.25 hours). Under the Section 9.2 conversion scale, what is the awarded CPD credit?
options: Three CPD hours (time spent >= 2.5 hrs and < 3.5 hrs).
Four CPD hours, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Two CPD hours, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
3.25 CPD hours, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 9.2: 3.25 hours falls in the band '>= 2.5 hrs < 3.5 hrs', which yields exactly 'Three CPD hours'.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: The Section 9.2 conversion table operates in discrete half-hour/hour brackets; alternative options miscalculate the applicable credit bracket.

question: Under Section 10.1 of APS 9 (v4.00), which of the following lists the mandatory minimum fields that must be maintained in an actuary's CPD record log?
options: Date, venue, speaker name, ticket invoice number, and employer signature, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

Member registration number, passport copy, hotel bills, and flight boarding passes, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

Date, name of event/activity, CPD hours claimed, area of practice, nature of activity (pre-approved vs other), classification (technical vs professional), learning outcomes description, and verifiable evidence.
Date, syllabus topic number, and IRDAI circular reference number, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Sections 10.1.1 through 10.1.8 enumerate the mandatory fields: Date, Name of event, Hours claimed, Area of practice, Nature (pre-approved vs other), Classification (technical vs professional), Learning outcomes description, and Verifiable evidence.
explanationIncorrect: Hotel bills, flight tickets, or IRDAI references are not the mandated fields of Section 10.1.

question: Under Section 10.1.7 of APS 9 (v4.00), what must be included in the 'description of learning outcomes' in the member's CPD log?
options: A signed certification from the actuary's direct line manager confirming attendance, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
A statement that the member found the session interesting and informative, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
A description of knowledge/skills gained, explaining how the activity contributed to professional development and fulfilled a personal development need commensurate with the hours recorded.
A transcript of every slide presented during the seminar, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 10.1.7 mandates: 'A brief description of learning outcomes providing a description of the knowledge and/or skills which the member gained as a result... Explanation should include how the activity contributed to professional development... and fulfilled a personal development need commensurate with the number of hours of CPD recorded.'
explanationIncorrect: Vague statements or administrative sign-offs do not satisfy the qualitative learning outcome standard of Section 10.1.7.

question: Under Section 10.1.9 to 10.1.15 of APS 9 (v4.00), which of the following is recognized as valid documentary evidence of participation in a CPD activity?
options: A verbal statement from a colleague who claims they saw the member at the venue, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
A personal calendar invite marked as 'accepted' on Microsoft Outlook, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
A debit card bank statement showing payment of delegate registration fees, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

A signed register of attendance; a completion certificate/letter/email; minutes of meeting listing attendees; published articles/papers; lecture hard copies with handwritten notes; or photographic/multimedia record with name on participant list.
explanationCorrect: Sections 10.1.10 to 10.1.15 specifically list: signed register, certificate/letter/email, minutes, published articles, presentation handouts with handwritten learning notes, or photographic/multimedia evidence with agenda/participant list.
explanationIncorrect: Outlook calendar invites, payment receipts alone without attendance proof, or verbal witness statements are not sufficient under Section 10.1.

question: An actuary writes a peer-reviewed research paper on longevity risk published in the 'Actuary India' magazine. Under Section 10.1.13 of APS 9 (v4.00), how does the actuary evidence this for CPD credit?
options: Articles or papers written for publication bearing the name of the member serve as valid documentary evidence.
The member must sit for a viva voce examination before the Education Committee.
The member must obtain a court affidavit confirming they are the true author.
Publication does not qualify for CPD under any circumstances, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 10.1.13 explicitly recognizes: 'Articles or papers written for publication bearing name of the member' as verifiable evidence of CPD.
explanationIncorrect: Affidavits or oral examinations are not required; the published paper bearing the member's name is sufficient documentary proof.

question: Under Section 10.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), for what minimum duration must a member preserve original physical or digital records of their CPD compliance?
options: At least three years aligned with Council election cycles, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
At least five years (e.g., records of FY 2020-21 must be preserved up to FY 2025-26) or for the period for which they held a valid CoP, whichever is lesser.
Permanently for the lifetime of the Fellow, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
At least one year until the subsequent self-attestation is accepted, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 10.2 specifies: 'The members must maintain the records of every CPD year for at least five years i.e. record of FY 20-21 should be preserved up to FY 25-26 (or for the period for which they would have held a valid CoP whichever is lesser)...'
explanationIncorrect: The retention period is at least 5 years, not 1 or 3 years.

question: An actuary who held a valid Certificate of Practice during FY 2021-22 surrenders their CoP in March 2023. In January 2026, the Institute conducts an audit of the actuary's FY 2021-22 CPD. Must the actuary still produce the records?
options: Yes; but only if the actuary is currently employed by a government body, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
No; the audit window closes exactly 12 months after CoP surrender, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Yes; because records of FY 2021-22 must be maintained for at least 5 years (up to FY 2026-27), the actuary is legally obligated to produce them upon request.

No; surrendering the CoP automatically extinguishes all historical audit liabilities, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under Section 10.2, records must be preserved for at least 5 years and 'must be made available to the IAI in the event it is asked for by the IAI as part of a process to audit compliance with CPD.'
explanationIncorrect: Surrendering a CoP does not erase past records maintenance obligations for periods during which the CoP was held.

question: By what deadline must a Category 2 member (active Fellow without CoP) submit their annual CPD self-attestation on the member's IAI portal under Section 11.1 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: Within six months of completion of the CPD year (by 30th September).
By 31st December at the end of the calendar year, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Within two months of completion of the relevant CPD year (i.e., by 31st May).
On the final day of the financial year (31st March), provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 11.1 specifies: 'Every member (other than Category 1) shall complete a self-attestation of their CPD records on the member's IAI portal within two months (i.e. by 31 May) of completion of the relevant CPD year.'
explanationIncorrect: The annual self-attestation deadline is strictly 31st May.

question: When must a Category 1 member (holding a CoP) complete their self-attestation of CPD records under Section 11.1 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: Whenever the member chooses during the subsequent two financial years.
Strictly on 31st May regardless of when CoP renewal occurs.
As of the date of CoP renewal or issuance of new CoP, whichever is earlier.
On 1st April in all circumstances, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Section 11.1 provides: 'For Category 1 it should be done as of date of CoP renewal or issuance of new CoP whichever is earlier.'
explanationIncorrect: Category 1 members attest as of the date of CoP renewal or issuance, whichever is earlier, aligning with the CoP licensing process.

question: The Institute selects a Fellow member's CPD declaration for routine compliance audit and issues an official request letter on 1st November. Under Section 11.4 of APS 9 (v4.00), within what timeframe must the member provide their records?
options: Within 30 calendar days, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Within 48 hours of email transmission, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Within 60 days concurrent with disciplinary defense filings, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Within 14 days of receipt of the request, or such other reasonable time as agreed by the Institute.
explanationCorrect: Section 11.4 strictly mandates: 'Members shall be required to provide their CPD records or any additional information in written or electronic form within 14 days of receipt of a request from the Institute or such other reasonable time as agreed by the Institute.'
explanationIncorrect: The statutory turnaround time for responding to a CPD audit notice is 14 days.

question: Under Section 11.5 of APS 9 (v4.00), what confidentiality protection is accorded to CPD records submitted by a member to the Institute during an audit?
options: Records are shared automatically with the member's employer and competing insurance companies, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Records are placed in the public domain under the Right to Information Act 2005, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Records will not be disclosed to other parties, except as necessary to conduct a compliance investigation or as part of a disciplinary investigation of the Institute.
Records are published immediately on the public website for peer review, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Section 11.5 provides: 'Any records provided to the Institute will not be disclosed to other parties, except as necessary to conduct an investigation of a Member's compliance with this Professional Standard or as part of a disciplinary investigation of the Institute.'
explanationIncorrect: Audit records are confidential and restricted strictly to compliance and disciplinary investigations.

question: If the Institute's review of a member's submitted CPD records reveals deficiencies or ambiguities, what is the mandatory initial procedural step under Section 11.5 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: The Institute will initially seek additional information from the member and provide him/her with a reasonable opportunity to fully document their records.
The Institute will suspend the member's CoP without notice, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
The Institute will levy an automatic administrative penalty of Rs. 50,000, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.

The Institute must immediately file a formal misconduct complaint before the Disciplinary Directorate, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Section 11.5 states: 'If, during examination of a Member's CPD records, the Institute has concerns about the adequacy of those records, it will initially seek additional information from that Member and provide him or her with a reasonable opportunity to fully document his or her records.'
explanationIncorrect: The Institute must first seek clarification and provide an opportunity to cure record deficiencies before initiating punitive actions.

question: On what date does the Institute publicly upload the names of members who are non-compliant with the CPD scheme onto the official IAI website under Section 12.2 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: On 1st July every year.
On 15th August on Independence Day.
On 1st June immediately following the 31st May attestation deadline.
On 31st March at the close of the financial year.
explanationCorrect: Section 12.2 explicitly provides: 'It shall be noted that members who are not compliant with the CPD scheme of the Institute, such member name will be uploaded on IAI website on 1st July every year and will be available until such time the member is compliant with CPD scheme...'
explanationIncorrect: Defaulters' names are uploaded publicly on 1st July each year.

question: How long does the name of a CPD non-compliant member remain published on the public IAI website under Section 12.2 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: For exactly 30 days, after which it must be automatically purged.
Until such time as the member becomes fully compliant with the CPD scheme of the Institute.
Permanently in the historical archives even after the member rectifies the default.
Until the conclusion of the next Annual General Meeting, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 12.2 states that the name 'will be available until such time the member is compliant with CPD scheme of the Institute.' Once the member cures their default, the name is removed.
explanationIncorrect: Removal is contingent on curing the non-compliance, not on fixed calendar expiries.

question: Under Section 12.2 of APS 9 (v4.00), what external action does the IAI take if a CPD non-compliant member holds membership in recognized foreign actuarial bodies (such as IFoA or SOA)?
options: The IAI has no authority to communicate with foreign bodies due to international data privacy treaties.
The IAI will demand that the foreign body automatically expel the member without an inquiry.
The IAI will inform the relevant foreign actuarial bodies about the member's CPD non-compliance.
The IAI will request the foreign body to seize the member's overseas bank accounts.
explanationCorrect: Section 12.2 states: 'Further, if they are member of other actuarial body/ies, such bodies would be informed accordingly about their CPD non-compliance.'
explanationIncorrect: Cross-border regulatory transparency mandates notifying foreign actuarial bodies of the member's non-compliant status.

question: Which of the following enforcement actions may the Institute take against a member who lacks reasonable grounds for CPD non-compliance under Section 12.1 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: Impose a mandatory criminal travel ban preventing the member from leaving the country, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Order the immediate attachment and liquidation of the member's residential property, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Sentence the member to civil imprisonment for up to 6 months, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Issue a warning letter; require further CPD within a timeframe; mandate quarterly reporting of CPD activities; and/or issue a warning of audit with potential disciplinary referral.
explanationCorrect: Sections 12.1.1 to 12.1.4 enumerate: warning letter, requiring further CPD evidence, requiring quarterly records, and warning of audit and potential referral under the Misconduct Rules 2008.
explanationIncorrect: Civil imprisonment, property attachment, or travel bans are criminal sanctions outside the statutory jurisdiction of the Institute.

question: Under Section 12.1.4 of APS 9 (v4.00), when do repeated breaches of CPD compliance escalate into formal disciplinary proceedings?
options: Repeated breaches result only in a doubled annual membership fee, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

Repeated breaches are automatically tried under the Indian Penal Code before a Sessions Judge, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

Repeated breaches can never trigger disciplinary action as CPD is purely voluntary, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Repeated breaches may constitute Actionable Conduct under the Actuaries (Procedure for Enquiry of Professional and Other Misconduct) Rules, 2008.
explanationCorrect: Section 12.1.4 specifies that if there are repeated breaches, 'this may constitute Actionable Conduct under the Institute's Disciplinary Scheme i.e The Actuaries (Procedure for enquiry of Professional an Other Misconduct) Rules, 2008.'
explanationIncorrect: Repeated CPD non-compliance is actionable professional misconduct under the 2008 Rules.

question: Under Section 12.1.5 of APS 9 (v4.00), how is a member's failure to comply with a Council direction regarding remedial CPD treated?
options: It automatically voids all actuarial valuation reports signed by the member over the past 10 years.
It is referred to the Quality Review Board for mandatory mediation.
It constitutes a further instance of Actionable Conduct under the IAI Disciplinary Scheme.
It is treated as a minor administrative oversight with no legal significance.
explanationCorrect: Section 12.1.5 explicitly establishes: 'Non-compliance with any direction by Council shall constitute further instance of Actionable Conduct under IAI Disciplinary Scheme.'
explanationIncorrect: Disobeying Council enforcement directions compounds professional misconduct.

question: An actuary who was CPD non-compliant for FY 2022-23 resigns from the Institute in August 2023. In 2025, the actuary applies for reinstatement of membership. Under Section 12.1.6, what must the actuary complete before reinstatement?
options: The actuary must re-take and pass the Actuarial Common Entrance Test (ACET), subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The actuary is permanently barred from reinstatement under the doctrine of estoppel.
The actuary must complete one full cycle of CPD before reinstatement of membership to be considered compliant.
The actuary must pay a penalty fee equal to 10 years of membership dues, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Section 12.1.6 mandates: 'Member who are not CPD Compliant for relevant CPD year and subsequently resigns or discontinue as members of the IAI and subsequently apply for reinstatement must complete one full cycle of CPD before reinstatement of membership...'
explanationIncorrect: Reinstatement after non-compliant resignation requires completing one full cycle of CPD.

question: Who has the statutory authority to issue binding clarifications and resolve any doubts related to the interpretation of APS 9 (v4.00) under Section 13?
options: The Council or the Committee authorised by the Council.
The High Court of Judicature at Bombay.
The external statutory auditor of the Institute.
The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI).
explanationCorrect: Section 13 (Removal of Doubts) states: 'For any doubt related to interpretation, the Council or Committee authorised by the Council is authorised to issue clarifications on the same.'
explanationIncorrect: The Council (or its authorised Committee) possesses sole interpretative authority.

question: Under Section 14.3 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the exact definition and CPD status of an 'Inactive Member'?
options: A member who has attained the age of 55 years; CPD is completely waived automatically, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

A member who continues to be on the register by paying subscription fees but is not in paid or unpaid work relying on actuarial training/experience in the widest interpretation, does not expect to return in foreseeable future; CPD is NOT mandatory for them.

A member who is unemployed for more than 3 consecutive months; CPD is halved, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Any member who takes a temporary vacation of more than 30 days; CPD is pro-rated, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Section 14.3 defines an inactive member as one who pays subscription fees but is not in paid or unpaid actuarial work in the widest interpretation and does not expect to return in foreseeable future; CPD requirements are not mandatory for them.
explanationIncorrect: Short vacations, temporary unemployment, or turning 55 do not automatically confer inactive status under Section 14.3.

question: A Fellow member retires from all commercial actuarial work and does not expect to return, but wishes to retain the prestigious 'FIAI' designation after their name. Under Section 4.6 of APS 9 (v4.00), what is the procedure to become a Category 3 member?
options: Send an SMS to the President of the Institute on the date of retirement, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Apply to the IAI at least 3 months before the end date of the annual membership year, pay prescribed fees, have membership in force, and submit the exemption form to the Compliance Officer.
Submit an affidavit to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Simply stop paying membership dues; inactive status is granted automatically, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.6 mandates that a member wishing to retain FIAI as an Inactive member must apply at least 3 months before the end of the membership year, pay prescribed fees, ensure membership is in force, and submit the form to yogesh@actuariesindia.org.
explanationIncorrect: Failing to pay dues leads to striking off, not inactive status. Formal written application 3 months prior is strictly required.

question: Once a Fellow is successfully registered as a Category 3 (Inactive) member under Section 4.6 of APS 9 (v4.00), what ongoing annual CPD reporting obligation remains?
options: They will no longer be required to confirm their status to the IAI each CPD year (nor complete annual CPD hours), provided membership is kept in force.
They must complete at least 6 hours of professional conduct CPD every year, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
They must attend the Annual General Meeting in person, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

They must still file an annual self-attestation stating 'Zero hours' by 31st May each year, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.6 provides: 'By doing so, they will no longer be required to confirm their status to the IAI each CPD year.'
explanationIncorrect: Category 3 members are relieved from annual CPD reporting and hourly requirements once registered.

question: To whom must the completed exemption application form for Category 3 or Category 4 status be submitted under Section 4.6 and 4.7 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: To the Chief Financial Officer of the Life Insurance Corporation of India.
To the Compliance Officer at yogesh@actuariesindia.org.
To the Chairperson of the Quality Review Board.
To the Secretary-General of the International Actuarial Association.
explanationCorrect: Sections 4.6, 4.7, and 4.8 explicitly state: 'Above category of members must complete the exemption application form and submit to Compliance Officer at yogesh@actuariesindia.org.'
explanationIncorrect: The designated submission officer is the Compliance Officer at the specified official email address.

question: A Fellow member decides to leave the actuarial profession entirely to pursue organic farming, does not expect to return, and does NOT wish to use the qualification 'FIAI' or continue membership. Under Section 4.7 of APS 9 (v4.00), what category applies and what is the legal effect?
options: Category 3: The member retains FIAI for life without paying dues, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Category 1: The member's CoP is transferred to their nearest surviving heir, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Category 2: The member remains liable for 15 CPD hours annually forever, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Category 4: Membership is discontinued from the date of application, and the member is NOT allowed to use the qualification 'FIAI' against their name.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.7 provides for Category 4: members who do not expect to return and do not wish to use FIAI or continue membership will have membership discontinued from the date of application and are not allowed to use FIAI.
explanationIncorrect: Category 3 allows retaining FIAI; Category 4 discontinues membership and strips the FIAI title.

question: A Fellow member (not holding a CoP) suffers a severe accident resulting in permanent physical disability certified at 45% by a medical board. Under Section 4.8 of APS 9 (v4.00), what relief is available regarding CPD?
options: The member may apply for an exemption from required CPD hours due to exceptional personal circumstances (permanent disability not less than 40%) by submitting an application to the Compliance Officer.
The member is automatically expelled from the Institute on medical grounds, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

The member is granted an automatic 50% discount on required CPD hours without needing to apply, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.

No relief is available because actuarial standards contain no provisions for medical disability, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.8 provides relief for members (other than Category 1) unable to meet CPD due to exceptional personal circumstances such as permanent disability (not less than 40%) or prolonged critical illness, upon application to yogesh@actuariesindia.org.
explanationIncorrect: Disability of 40% or more qualifies for exemption application; relief is not automatic and requires formal submission.

question: Can an Appointed Actuary holding a valid Certificate of Practice (Category 1) claim an exemption from CPD under the exceptional personal circumstances / permanent disability clause of Section 4.8 of APS 9 (v4.00)?
options: Yes; but only if the Appointed Actuary appoints a student actuary to act on their behalf, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
No; Section 4.8 explicitly restricts medical/disability exemption applications to 'Fellow members other than Category 1'. A practicing actuary holding a CoP cannot claim this exemption.
Yes; provided the IRDAI approves the waiver in writing, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Yes; any member regardless of category can claim an exemption upon producing a medical certificate, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.8 begins: 'Fellow members other than Category 1 who are unable to meet the required CPD hours due to exceptional personal circumstances...'. Category 1 CoP holders are strictly ineligible for Section 4.8 waivers.
explanationIncorrect: A practicing actuary holding a CoP cannot sign statutory certificates while claiming medical incapacity from fulfilling basic professional currency.

question: A Fellow member practicing in the United Kingdom holds Fellowship in both the IAI and the Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (IFoA). Under Section 4.5.1 of APS 9 (v4.00), what must this Category 2 member do to claim an exemption from IAI CPD?
options: Sit for the Indian Business Law exam annually, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Pay an overseas waiver fee of GBP 500 to the IAI accounts department, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Declare at the start of the CPD year that the IFoA is their primary body, meet IFoA CPD requirements (which are equivalent/greater), and submit confirmation/certificate from the IFoA.

Simply assume they are exempt because dual Fellows never need to report to the IAI, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.5.1 requires the member to: (1) be a fellow of a recognized body; (2) meet CPD equivalent/greater than IAI; (3) declare at the start of the CPD year that the other body is primary; and (4) submit confirmation/certificate from that body.
explanationIncorrect: Exemption is not passive; timely declaration at the start of the year and third-party verification are mandatory.

question: If a Category 2 member claiming an overseas body exemption under Section 4.5.1 fails to submit the confirmation/certificate from the foreign actuarial body, how does the IAI treat the member?
options: The member's Indian citizenship is revoked, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
The exemption is denied, and the member is treated as non-compliant with standard IAI Category 2 CPD requirements (15 hours).
The member is granted an automatic 3-year extension under international comity, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
The foreign actuarial body is fined by the IAI, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Failure to substantiate the foreign compliance certificate invalidates the mutual recognition claim, leaving the member subject to standard Category 2 compliance default.
explanationIncorrect: Exemptions require strict documentary substantiation under Section 4.5.1.

question: An actuary prepares and delivers a 2-hour technical lecture on machine learning in mortality forecasting at an IAI Global Conference of Actuaries. Under Section 10.1.14 of APS 9, what documentary evidence must the actuary retain to verify their learning?
options: A screenshot of the PowerPoint icon on their desktop computer, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Hard copies of lectures or presentations, including hand-written learning notes by the member.
A written thank-you note from an audience member, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Only the commercial flyer distributed before the conference, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Section 10.1.14 explicitly specifies: 'Hard copies of lectures or presentations, including hand-written learning notes by the member' as verifiable evidence.
explanationIncorrect: Flyers or desktop icons do not prove presentation delivery or personal learning notes.

question: Under Section 10.1.15 of APS 9 (v4.00), when can photographic or multimedia records be utilized as valid verifiable evidence of CPD participation?
options: Whenever an actuary takes a selfie outside the conference hall building, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Only if the photograph is published on the front page of a national newspaper, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
When the photographic or multimedia record of participation is accompanied by the member's name on an agenda or participants list of the event.
Photographs are never accepted as evidence under any circumstances, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Section 10.1.15 recognizes: 'Photographic or other multimedia record of participation together with name on an agenda or participants list of an event.'
explanationIncorrect: Unsubstantiated selfies without official agenda/participant listings do not satisfy Section 10.1.15.

question: An Appointed Actuary in Life Insurance attends 12 hours of pre-approved technical Life sessions, 4 hours of pre-approved General Insurance sessions, 6 hours of professional conduct sessions, and 2 hours of other verifiable reading during FY 2024-25. Can the 4 GI hours help meet the mandatory 15-hour technical Life requirement under APS 9?
options: No; attending General Insurance events is strictly forbidden for Life actuaries, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Yes; any actuarial technical hours can be pooled together indiscriminately, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

Yes; provided the Appointed Actuary writes a memo stating GI techniques are applicable to Life, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

No; under Section 4.4.3(1), the minimum 15 technical CPD hours must be in the member's specific area of practice (Life Insurance). The 4 GI hours cannot dilute or substitute for the core 15 Life hours.
explanationCorrect: Section 4.4.3(1) mandates: 'A minimum of 15 CPD hours should be pre-approved verifiable technical CPD hours in specific area of practice.' Cross-practice hours cannot substitute for the mandatory primary practice quota.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Section 4.4.3 mandates a strict portfolio breakdown of at least 15 technical pre-approved hours, at least 6 professional hours, and up to 3 other hours. Alternative options distort this statutory allocation.

question: A Fellow member in Category 2 claims 9 hours of pre-approved technical CPD, 2 hours of professional conduct CPD, and 4 hours of other verifiable CPD (total 15 hours). When reviewing this under Section 4.5, what compliance deficiency exists?
options: Technical hours are deficient by 6 hours because 15 are always required, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
