options: Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Setting opening Contractual Service Margin (CSM) equal to historical gross premiums or arbitrarily assigning zero CSM at transition without fair value calibration violates Ind AS 117 Para C20 and Ind AS 113. Under the Fair Value approach, the opening CSM is determined as the difference between the fair value of the group of contracts and its fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.

Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming that sovereign or private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk, or omitting an explicit probability-of-default haircut from reinsurance asset valuation, violates Ind AS 117 Para 63. Actuaries must incorporate a forward-looking allowance for expected reinsurance counterparty non-performance reflecting rating downgrades, disputes, and recovery delays.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.

Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Accepting actuarial claims development triangles without reconciling them against audited financial accounting general ledgers violates ICAI SA 500 (Audit Evidence) and SA 620. Actuaries and auditing teams cannot rely blindly on unverified operational data extracts; data integrity and completeness reconciliations are mandatory audit preconditions.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Super-Imposed Judicial Inflation in Motor TP (Sec 5.17))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is projecting future claim inflation for motor bodily injury claims. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Apply a negative inflation rate to compress long-tail reserving deficits, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming zero future claim inflation or relying solely on general headline consumer price index (CPI) fails to recognize super-imposed judicial inflation, where Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) court awards and specialized bodily injury medical costs escalate significantly faster than headline CPI. Applying a negative inflation rate artificially suppresses liabilities, violating Ind AS 117 measurement standards and constituting severe audit non-compliance.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Bundling distinct non-insurance components (such as roadside assistance, wellness device subscriptions, or asset management services) into insurance liabilities distorts revenue timing. Under Ind AS 117 Para 12, distinct goods or services must be unbundled and accounted for under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during the first-time adoption audit of Ind AS 117 for a composite reinsurer, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Omitting the mandatory roll-forward reconciliations of insurance contract liabilities between opening and closing balances impairs transparency and breaches Ind AS 117 Para 100. Actuaries must disclose detailed movements across estimates of future cash flows, the risk adjustment for non-financial risk, and the contractual service margin.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65 and FT-IGN 31, only costs directly attributable to acquiring the specific portfolio of insurance contracts can be recognized within fulfilment cash flows. Capitalizing corporate general overheads, headquarters rent, executive salaries, or general marketing and brand sponsorships violates statutory accounting, which requires indirect overheads to be expensed immediately in profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Concealing financial options or guarantees within general insurance liabilities without separate assessment, or failing to bifurcate embedded investment derivatives under Ind AS 109, distorts the insurer's balance sheet volatility and solvency reporting. Actuaries must bifurcate and fair-value distinct financial derivatives whose economic characteristics and risks are not closely related to the host contract.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Foreign Exchange Accounting (Ind AS 21 & 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is auditing foreign currency denominated insurance contracts in GIFT City. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Crediting foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves, ignoring currency movements, or failing to retranslate monetary insurance liabilities at the closing spot rate directly violates Ind AS 21 and Ind AS 117. Insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary liabilities and all exchange differences must be recognized in the statement of profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Interim Accounting Policy Choice (Para B137))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of a foreign reinsurance branch (FRB) operating in Mumbai, the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.

Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Changing accounting policy choices between interim reporting periods to manipulate quarterly earnings, or smoothing reported results across quarters, violates Ind AS 117 Para B137 and Ind AS 34. Entities must apply their chosen accounting policy (whether to change treatment of previous accounting estimates made in previous interim periods) consistently across all interim reporting periods.

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during an audit where the Appointed Actuary vigorously defends existing reserves, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Omitting the mandatory roll-forward reconciliations of insurance contract liabilities between opening and closing balances impairs transparency and breaches Ind AS 117 Para 100. Actuaries must disclose detailed movements across estimates of future cash flows, the risk adjustment for non-financial risk, and the contractual service margin.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.

Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65 and FT-IGN 31, only costs directly attributable to acquiring the specific portfolio of insurance contracts can be recognized within fulfilment cash flows. source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Concealing financial options or guarantees within general insurance liabilities without separate assessment, or failing to bifurcate embedded investment derivatives under Ind AS 109, distorts the insurer's balance sheet volatility and solvency reporting. Actuaries must bifurcate and fair-value distinct financial derivatives whose economic characteristics and risks are not closely related to the host contract.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Foreign Exchange Accounting (Ind AS 21 & 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is auditing foreign currency denominated insurance contracts in GIFT City. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.

Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.

Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Crediting foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves, ignoring currency movements, or failing to retranslate monetary insurance liabilities at the closing spot rate directly violates Ind AS 21 and Ind AS 117. Insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary liabilities and all exchange differences must be recognized in the statement of profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Interim Accounting Policy Choice (Para B137))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.

Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.

Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Changing accounting policy choices between interim reporting periods to manipulate quarterly earnings, or smoothing reported results across quarters, violates Ind AS 117 Para B137 and Ind AS 34. Entities must apply their chosen accounting policy (whether to change treatment of previous accounting estimates made in previous interim periods) consistently across all interim reporting periods.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Transition Fair Value Model (Para C20))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening CSM determined under the Fair Value Approach at transition. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Setting opening Contractual Service Margin (CSM) equal to historical gross premiums or arbitrarily assigning zero CSM at transition without fair value calibration violates Ind AS 117 Para C20 and Ind AS 113. Under the Fair Value approach, the opening CSM is determined as the difference between the fair value of the group of contracts and its fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.
Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming that sovereign or private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk, or omitting an explicit probability-of-default haircut from reinsurance asset valuation, violates Ind AS 117 Para 63. Actuaries must incorporate a forward-looking allowance for expected reinsurance counterparty non-performance reflecting rating downgrades, disputes, and recovery delays.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.

Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Accepting actuarial claims development triangles without reconciling them against audited financial accounting general ledgers violates ICAI SA 500 (Audit Evidence) and SA 620. Actuaries and auditing teams cannot rely blindly on unverified operational data extracts; data integrity and completeness reconciliations are mandatory audit preconditions.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Super-Imposed Judicial Inflation in Motor TP (Sec 5.17))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where executive bonuses are tied to reported net profit targets, the actuarial audit team is projecting future claim inflation for motor bodily injury claims. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Apply a negative inflation rate to compress long-tail reserving deficits, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming zero future claim inflation or relying solely on general headline consumer price index (CPI) fails to recognize super-imposed judicial inflation, where Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) court awards and specialized bodily injury medical costs escalate significantly faster than headline CPI. Applying a negative inflation rate artificially suppresses liabilities, violating Ind AS 117 measurement standards and constituting severe audit non-compliance.

options: Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Setting opening Contractual Service Margin (CSM) equal to historical gross premiums or arbitrarily assigning zero CSM at transition without fair value calibration violates Ind AS 117 Para C20 and Ind AS 113. source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where internal actuarial models were recently migrated to cloud infrastructure, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.

Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where internal actuarial models were recently migrated to cloud infrastructure, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. options: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.

Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Super-Imposed Judicial Inflation in Motor TP (Sec 5.17))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where internal actuarial models were recently migrated to cloud infrastructure, the actuarial audit team is projecting future claim inflation for motor bodily injury claims. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Apply a negative inflation rate to compress long-tail reserving deficits, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming zero future claim inflation or relying solely on general headline consumer price index (CPI) fails to recognize super-imposed judicial inflation, where Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) court awards and specialized bodily injury medical costs escalate significantly faster than headline CPI. Applying a negative inflation rate artificially suppresses liabilities, violating Ind AS 117 measurement standards and constituting severe audit non-compliance.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where internal actuarial models were recently migrated to cloud infrastructure, the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Bundling distinct non-insurance components (such as roadside assistance, wellness device subscriptions, or asset management services) into insurance liabilities distorts revenue timing. Under Ind AS 117 Para 12, distinct goods or services must be unbundled and accounted for under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit where internal actuarial models were recently migrated to cloud infrastructure, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Omitting the mandatory roll-forward reconciliations of insurance contract liabilities between opening and closing balances impairs transparency and breaches Ind AS 117 Para 100. Actuaries must disclose detailed movements across estimates of future cash flows, the risk adjustment for non-financial risk, and the contractual service margin.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a special audit review mandated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI), the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65 and FT-IGN 31, only costs directly attributable to acquiring the specific portfolio of insurance contracts can be recognized within fulfilment cash flows. Capitalizing corporate general overheads, headquarters rent, executive salaries, or general marketing and brand sponsorships violates statutory accounting, which requires indirect overheads to be expensed immediately in profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a special audit review mandated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI), the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Concealing financial options or guarantees within general insurance liabilities without separate assessment, or failing to bifurcate embedded investment derivatives under Ind AS 109, distorts the insurer's balance sheet volatility and solvency reporting. Actuaries must bifurcate and fair-value distinct financial derivatives whose economic characteristics and risks are not closely related to the host contract.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Foreign Exchange Accounting (Ind AS 21 & 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), during a special audit review mandated by the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI), the actuarial audit team is auditing foreign currency denominated insurance contracts in GIFT City. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Crediting foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves, ignoring currency movements, or failing to retranslate monetary insurance liabilities at the closing spot rate directly violates Ind AS 21 and Ind AS 117. Insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary liabilities and all exchange differences must be recognized in the statement of profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of an insurer writing specialized cyber and environmental liability policies, the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Bundling distinct non-insurance components (such as roadside assistance, wellness device subscriptions, or asset management services) into insurance liabilities distorts revenue timing. Under Ind AS 117 Para 12, distinct goods or services must be unbundled and accounted for under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit of an insurer writing specialized cyber and environmental liability policies, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Omitting the mandatory roll-forward reconciliations of insurance contract liabilities between opening and closing balances impairs transparency and breaches Ind AS 117 Para 100. Actuaries must disclose detailed movements across estimates of future cash flows, the risk adjustment for non-financial risk, and the contractual service margin.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65 and FT-IGN 31, only costs directly attributable to acquiring the specific portfolio of insurance contracts can be recognized within fulfilment cash flows. Capitalizing corporate general overheads, headquarters rent, executive salaries, or general marketing and brand sponsorships violates statutory accounting, which requires indirect overheads to be expensed immediately in profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Concealing financial options or guarantees within general insurance liabilities without separate assessment, or failing to bifurcate embedded investment derivatives under Ind AS 109, distorts the insurer's balance sheet volatility and solvency reporting. Actuaries must bifurcate and fair-value distinct financial derivatives whose economic characteristics and risks are not closely related to the host contract.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Foreign Exchange Accounting (Ind AS 21 & 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is auditing foreign currency denominated insurance contracts in GIFT City. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Crediting foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves, ignoring currency movements, or failing to retranslate monetary insurance liabilities at the closing spot rate directly violates Ind AS 21 and Ind AS 117. Insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary liabilities and all exchange differences must be recognized in the statement of profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Interim Accounting Policy Choice (Para B137))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Changing accounting policy choices between interim reporting periods to manipulate quarterly earnings, or smoothing reported results across quarters, violates Ind AS 117 Para B137 and Ind AS 34. Entities must apply their chosen accounting policy (whether to change treatment of previous accounting estimates made in previous interim periods) consistently across all interim reporting periods.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Transition Fair Value Model (Para C20))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening CSM determined under the Fair Value Approach at transition. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Setting opening Contractual Service Margin (CSM) equal to historical gross premiums or arbitrarily assigning zero CSM at transition without fair value calibration violates Ind AS 117 Para C20 and Ind AS 113. Under the Fair Value approach, the opening CSM is determined as the difference between the fair value of the group of contracts and its fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.
Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.

Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming that sovereign or private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk, or omitting an explicit probability-of-default haircut from reinsurance asset valuation, violates Ind AS 117 Para 63. Actuaries must incorporate a forward-looking allowance for expected reinsurance counterparty non-performance reflecting rating downgrades, disputes, and recovery delays.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing a group micro-insurance portfolio distributed through rural cooperative banks, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. options: Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.

Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.

options: Ignore currency fluctuations by assuming 1 US Dollar equals 1 Indian Rupee in financial books, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.

Credit all foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves while expensing losses, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
Prohibit foreign currency valuation in all Indian financial statements, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Treat insurance contracts as monetary items; foreign exchange differences on fulfilment cash flows and CSM flow to P&L under Ind AS 21.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Crediting foreign exchange gains directly to general reserves, ignoring currency movements, or failing to retranslate monetary insurance liabilities at the closing spot rate directly violates Ind AS 21 and Ind AS 117. Insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary liabilities and all exchange differences must be recognized in the statement of profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Interim Accounting Policy Choice (Para B137))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is evaluating quarterly financial reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.

Change interim accounting policies every quarter to maximize reported interim profits, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Prohibit insurance companies from issuing quarterly financial statements, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.

Recalculate all prior interim reports from scratch whenever annual numbers are published, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify whether the entity has elected not to reverse previous interim estimates, and confirm consistent year-on-year application.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Changing accounting policy choices between interim reporting periods to manipulate quarterly earnings, or smoothing reported results across quarters, violates Ind AS 117 Para B137 and Ind AS 34. Entities must apply their chosen accounting policy (whether to change treatment of previous accounting estimates made in previous interim periods) consistently across all interim reporting periods.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Transition Fair Value Model (Para C20))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening CSM determined under the Fair Value Approach at transition. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Use US GAAP book value of equity as the opening CSM balance, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
Set opening CSM to exactly zero for all historical insurance policies without valuation.
Set opening CSM equal to total historical gross premiums collected since company inception.
Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify opening CSM reflects the difference between Ind AS 113 fair value and fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Setting opening Contractual Service Margin (CSM) equal to historical gross premiums or arbitrarily assigning zero CSM at transition without fair value calibration violates Ind AS 117 Para C20 and Ind AS 113. Under the Fair Value approach, the opening CSM is determined as the difference between the fair value of the group of contracts and its fulfilment cash flows at the transition date.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Reinsurance Counterparty Default Haircuts (Para 63))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is auditing expected credit loss provisions on reinsurance assets. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Deduct an arbitrary 90% penalty from all foreign reinsurer receivables regardless of rating.
Assume sovereign and private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk under all conditions.
Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.

Record credit losses only after a reinsurer is officially declared bankrupt by a court, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify that future cash flows reflect an explicit probability-weighted allowance for reinsurer credit default and dispute haircuts.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming that sovereign or private reinsurers carry zero credit default risk, or omitting an explicit probability-of-default haircut from reinsurance asset valuation, violates Ind AS 117 Para 63. Actuaries must incorporate a forward-looking allowance for expected reinsurance counterparty non-performance reflecting rating downgrades, disputes, and recovery delays.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Claims Development Triangles Reconciliation (SA 500))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is verifying historical claims triangles against accounting ledgers. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.

Replace triangle data with theoretical Poisson simulation models without ledger cross-checks, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Accept claims triangles without reconciliation because actuarial databases are always accurate.
Delete older accident years from triangles if claims ratios were unfavorable, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Reconcile cumulative paid and incurred claims triangles against audited financial general ledgers, investigating any unmapped variance.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Accepting actuarial claims development triangles without reconciling them against audited financial accounting general ledgers violates ICAI SA 500 (Audit Evidence) and SA 620. Actuaries and auditing teams cannot rely blindly on unverified operational data extracts; data integrity and completeness reconciliations are mandatory audit preconditions.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Super-Imposed Judicial Inflation in Motor TP (Sec 5.17))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is projecting future claim inflation for motor bodily injury claims. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Apply headline consumer price index (CPI) assuming court awards are legally capped by inflation targets.
Apply a negative inflation rate to compress long-tail reserving deficits, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
Assume zero future inflation on the premise that Indian tort law will freeze compensation awards.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Incorporate judicial award escalation and medical cost inflation, recognizing that court awards rise faster than headline CPI.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Assuming zero future claim inflation or relying solely on general headline consumer price index (CPI) fails to recognize super-imposed judicial inflation, where Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (MACT) court awards and specialized bodily injury medical costs escalate significantly faster than headline CPI. Applying a negative inflation rate artificially suppresses liabilities, violating Ind AS 117 measurement standards and constituting severe audit non-compliance.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Unbundling Distinct Non-Insurance Goods & Services (Para 12))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is auditing annual maintenance and concierge services sold with insurance. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Treat the entire contract as a non-financial service contract, voiding insurance accounting.
Ignore the non-insurance service because ancillary benefits carry zero accounting weight.
Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
Bundle all goods and services into insurance liabilities to delay revenue recognition.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Unbundle the distinct non-insurance service and measure it under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Bundling distinct non-insurance components (such as roadside assistance, wellness device subscriptions, or asset management services) into insurance liabilities distorts revenue timing. Under Ind AS 117 Para 12, distinct goods or services must be unbundled and accounted for under Ind AS 115 (Revenue from Contracts with Customers).

question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), in an audit review following a major catastrophic flood event triggering reinsurance disputes, the actuarial audit team is auditing opening-to-closing reconciliations of LRC, LIC, and CSM. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Allow management to omit roll-forward tables to protect confidential company margin information.
Disclose roll-forward reconciliations only once every ten years, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.
Present roll-forward reconciliations using unverified handwritten notes, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Verify comprehensive roll-forward tables detailing insurance revenue, finance expenses, cash flows, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Omitting the mandatory roll-forward reconciliations of insurance contract liabilities between opening and closing balances impairs transparency and breaches Ind AS 117 Para 100. Actuaries must disclose detailed movements across estimates of future cash flows, the risk adjustment for non-financial risk, and the contractual service margin.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Acquisition Expense Direct Attribution (Para B65))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing financial statements submitted for an upcoming initial public offering (IPO), the actuarial audit team is allocating distribution channel costs to contract groups. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Acquisition costs must be amortized over a flat 100-year schedule, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
All corporate executive entertainment and luxury travel expenses are capitalized into contract cash flows.
Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
Zero acquisition costs can be recognized under Indian accounting standards, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Only directly attributable costs incurred to acquire the specific portfolio are included in fulfilment cash flows; corporate overheads are expensed.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65 and FT-IGN 31, only costs directly attributable to acquiring the specific portfolio of insurance contracts can be recognized within fulfilment cash flows. Capitalizing corporate general overheads, headquarters rent, executive salaries, or general marketing and brand sponsorships violates statutory accounting, which requires indirect overheads to be expensed immediately in profit or loss.

source: FT-IGN 31 Audit Practice (Embedded Derivatives Bifurcation (Ind AS 109 vs 117))
question: Under FT-IGN 31 (Auditing Actuary under Ind AS 117 & ICAI SA 620), while auditing financial statements submitted for an upcoming initial public offering (IPO), the actuarial audit team is evaluating guaranteed equity returns in structured contracts. What is the correct professional requirement?
options: Reclassify the entire insurance company as an unregulated hedge fund, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Prohibit the issuance of any contract containing investment features, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.

Always conceal the derivative within general insurance reserves without separate disclosure, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 and ICAI SA 620, the correct audit procedure is: Bifurcate and measure under Ind AS 109 at fair value through P&L if economic characteristics are not closely related to the host contract.
explanationIncorrect: Distractor analysis: Concealing financial options or guarantees within general insurance liabilities without separate assessment, or failing to bifurcate embedded investment derivatives under Ind AS 109, distorts the insurer's balance sheet volatility and solvency reporting. Actuaries must bifurcate and fair-value distinct financial derivatives whose economic characteristics and risks are not closely related to the host contract.
