Include claims handling expenses only if claims occurred more than 10 years ago, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para B65(f) and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.10, LIC fulfillment cash flows must include all direct claims handling expenses expected to be incurred to settle both outstanding reported claims and IBNR.
explanationIncorrect: Omitting claims handling expenses materially understates the Liability for Incurred Claims.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.53 (Currency Translation & Foreign Exchange Impact on CSM)
question: Where an Indian insurer issues policies denominated in foreign currencies (e.g. GIFT City IFSC branch), how is foreign exchange audited under Ind AS 117 Para 30 and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.12?
options: Insurance contracts in foreign currencies are treated as monetary items; exchange differences on fulfillment cash flows and CSM are recognized in P&L under Ind AS 21.

Foreign exchange variations are ignored by assuming all global currencies equal the Indian Rupee, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

Foreign currency contracts are strictly illegal and cannot be audited in India, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Exchange differences are paid to the International Monetary Fund (IMF), provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
explanationCorrect: Under Ind AS 117 Para 30 and Ind AS 21, insurance contracts denominated in foreign currencies are monetary items; foreign exchange changes on cash flows and CSM are recognized in P&L.
explanationIncorrect: Misclassifying foreign currency exchange shifts as CSM unlocking distorts foreign exchange gains/losses.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.55 (Interim Financial Reporting under Ind AS 34 and Ind AS 117)
question: Under Ind AS 117 Para B137 and FT-IGN 31 Section 7.14, what is the accounting policy choice available to Indian insurers regarding treatment of previous interim accounting estimates?
options: Interim reports are strictly forbidden for insurance companies under Indian law, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
An entity must recalculate all interim periods from scratch using hindsight, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.

An entity may elect an accounting policy choice not to change the treatment of accounting estimates made in previous interim periods when applying Ind AS 117 in subsequent interim periods or annual reports.
Interim reports must be signed exclusively by the Ministry of Finance, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para B137 provides an accounting policy choice regarding whether previous interim period estimates are reversed in subsequent periods; the Auditing Actuary must verify that this policy is applied consistently.
explanationIncorrect: Inconsistent application of interim accounting policy choices across quarters distorts annual comparisons.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.57 (Mandatory Reconciliation Disclosures under Para 100)
question: What critical reconciliation disclosures must the Auditing Actuary audit in the notes to the financial statements under Ind AS 117 Para 100?
options: A list of all policyholder email passwords, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
A reconciliation of the number of chairs and desks in the actuary's office, subject to approval by the Competent Authority under the prescribed statutory administrative framework.
Reconciliation disclosures are optional suggestions that insurers may omit, provided the member executes an indemnity agreement and discloses the procedural limitation to all intended users.

Detailed reconciliations from opening to closing balances for the Liability for Remaining Coverage (LRC), Liability for Incurred Claims (LIC), and Contractual Service Margin (CSM), showing key drivers of movement.
explanationCorrect: Ind AS 117 Para 100 mandates comprehensive roll-forward reconciliations showing how insurance liabilities and CSM moved from opening to closing balance, detailing cash flows, revenue, finance expense, and assumption changes.
explanationIncorrect: Incomplete or missing roll-forward reconciliations constitute material disclosure non-compliance.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 6.59 (Cold Review Findings: Root Cause Analysis & Remediation)
question: When internal cold quality reviews identify recurring deficiencies in an actuarial audit engagement under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.2, what must the firm do?
options: Destroy the cold review report and pretend no deficiencies were found, on the premise that formal written notification has been submitted to the Council under the relevant statutory provisions.
Conduct a root cause analysis, implement remedial actions (enhanced training, updated audit programs, mandatory partner re-briefing), and monitor effectiveness in subsequent audit cycles.
Dismiss the cold reviewer from employment for being excessively critical, provided an independent peer review is conducted and formal approval is documented under applicable professional guidelines.
Increase audit fees by 50% to penalize the client for the audit firm's defects, subject to prior written authorization from the Board Audit Committee and prominent disclosure in the final report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.2 and ICAI SQC 1, systemic audit defects identified during cold quality reviews require formal root cause analysis, corrective action plans, and firm-wide remediation.
explanationIncorrect: Ignoring cold review findings undermines audit firm quality controls and exposes the firm to disciplinary action by the QRB.

source: FT-IGN 31, Section 8.4 (Audit Re-Performance Testing & Tolerance Thresholds)
question: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.4, what is the protocol when the Auditing Actuary conducts independent re-performance of liability calculations?
options: Require the insurer to match the auditor's numbers to the exact single rupee, permitting zero variance, unless the terms of reference specifically mandate an independent peer review under Actuarial Practice Standard 34.
Conduct re-performance only if the insurer pays an additional bonus fee, provided the actuary can demonstrate that the deviation produces an immaterial financial effect on reported liabilities.
Re-perform calculations on independent calculation platforms, establish pre-defined acceptable variance thresholds (tolerances), and thoroughly investigate any variance exceeding the threshold.

Accept any difference up to 50% of the company's total assets without investigation, provided the full quantifiable financial impact and risk assessment are prominently disclosed in the actuarial report.
explanationCorrect: Under FT-IGN 31 Section 8.4 and SA 620, re-performance testing requires clear pre-established tolerance limits; variances exceeding tolerance must be reconciled to identify underlying model or parameter causes.
explanationIncorrect: Ignoring differences that exceed established audit tolerances compromises the reliability of audit evidence.
